articles.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and deputy secretary of state, has died
articles.dek: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.

paragraphs.en: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.
paragraphs.zh: 斯特罗布·塔尔博特，一位曾任《时代》杂志记者，后来在比尔·克林顿总统任内担任副国务卿，并随后领导布鲁金斯学会的人，于周四去世。他享年80岁。

paragraphs.en: His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he passed away peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home.
paragraphs.zh: 他的儿子德文·塔尔博特证实，他在纽约东汉普顿的家中，经过长期病痛后平静地去世。

paragraphs.en: The elder Talbott was educated at Yale and Oxford, where he bunked with Clinton. While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former first secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union who was ousted in 1964.
paragraphs.zh: 年长的塔尔博特曾在耶鲁和牛津受教育，在那里他与克林顿同住宿舍。在英国大学期间，在莫斯科为《时代》杂志实习后，该杂志要求塔尔博特协助翻译尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫的泄露回忆录，赫鲁晓夫是苏联共产党前第一书记，1964年被免职。

paragraphs.en: Talbott did, and it gave him some notoriety as a young man and a job at the magazine.
paragraphs.zh: Talbott 确实这样做了，这让他作为一个年轻人获得了一些名声，也在那本杂志上找到了工作。

paragraphs.en: After 21 years at Time, where he focused on Soviet-American relations and held positions including Washington bureau chief and a foreign-affairs columnist, according to his U.S. State Department biography, he received a call from the newly elected Clinton.
paragraphs.zh: 据美国国务院的简历，他在《时代》工作21年，专注于苏美关系，并担任包括华盛顿分社社长和外交事务专栏作家等职位，他接到了新当选的克林顿的电话。

paragraphs.en: Talbott joined the U.S. State Department in 1994, swiftly becoming deputy secretary of state. In that role, he was the architect of the Clinton administration's approach to Russia and other formerly Soviet countries and conducted negotiations between the U.S. and India after the latter's nuclear tests in 1998.
paragraphs.zh: 塔尔博特于1994年加入美国国务院，很快就成为副国务卿。在这一职务上，他是克林顿政府对俄罗斯及其他前苏联国家政策的设计者，并在1998年印度进行核试验后主持了美印之间的谈判。

paragraphs.en: "Strobe was a good and brilliant man who made our world more peaceful and secure," said Clinton in a statement after Talbott's death. When Talbott was translating Khrushchev's memoirs while at Oxford, it was Clinton's job to make him breakfast every day, he said, adding, "somehow, I got the better end of the deal."
paragraphs.zh: “斯特罗布是一个善良而聪明的人，他让我们的世界更加和平与安全，”克林顿在塔尔博特去世后的一份声明中说。他表示，当塔尔博特在牛津翻译赫鲁晓夫的回忆录时，他的工作是每天为塔尔博特准备早餐，并补充道，“不知怎的，我在这笔交易中占了上风。”

paragraphs.en: Both he and Hillary were "deeply saddened" by the passing of "a wonderful friend, and a world-class human being," he said.
paragraphs.zh: 他说，他和希拉里都因“一位了不起的朋友和世界级的人”的去世而“深感悲痛”。

articles.title: How Jensen Huang's return as NVIDIA's CEO is going over in China
articles.dek: In China, Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO is being met with a mixed reaction – as Beijing weighs whether it wants the US company's chips at all.

paragraphs.en: In China, Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO is being met with a mixed reaction – as Beijing weighs whether it wants the US company's chips at all.
paragraphs.zh: 在中国，黄仁勋重返英伟达首席执行官一职的消息引起了复杂的反响——北京正在权衡是否真正需要这家美国公司的芯片。

paragraphs.en: Jensen Huang now has his job back at NVIDIA. Whether China should have access to NVIDIA's best computer chips - that debate is now back, too. And how is all this playing out in China? Well, we've reached NPR's Jennifer Pak in Beijing. Hi there.
paragraphs.zh: 黄仁勋现在已经重新在英伟达上班了。关于中国是否应该能够使用英伟达最好的电脑芯片——这一争论现在也回来了。那这一切在中国的发展情况如何呢？我们现在连线到了在北京的NPR记者詹妮弗·帕克。你好。

paragraphs.en: SUMMERS: Jennifer, you're there in Beijing. Tell us what you've been hearing from people.
paragraphs.zh: 萨默斯：詹妮弗，你现在在北京。告诉我们你从人们那里听到了什么。

paragraphs.en: PAK: Well, from the general public, some say this whole saga of Jensen Huang's swift fall and sudden return is kind of like a microdrama. I don't know if you're familiar with these. These are super popular, kind of like soap operas. They're broken down into bite-size episodes, two to three minutes each, super fast pace. And just like a microdrama, this Huang scandal has had a lot of twists and turns.
paragraphs.zh: PAK：嗯，从公众的角度来看，有人说黄仁勋迅速下台又突然复出的整个事件有点像一个微型剧。我不知道你是否熟悉这些东西。这些非常受欢迎，有点像肥皂剧。它们被分解成小片段，每集两到三分钟，节奏非常快。就像一部微型剧一样，这场黄氏丑闻也经历了很多曲折。

paragraphs.en: In China's tech circles, the views are split. I spoke to Du Chen, a technology media editor at Ifanr in Beijing. He says one group believes Huang's conduct raises serious ethical violations and shouldn't be in charge. While the other group, he says, are ones who have had business dealings with NVIDIA or interacted with Huang directly and indirectly.
paragraphs.zh: 在中国的科技圈里，观点分歧。我在北京采访了爱范儿的科技媒体编辑杜晨。他表示，一部分人认为黄的行为涉及严重的道德违规，不应该担任领导职务。而另一部分人，他说，是那些与英伟达有过业务往来或直接、间接与黄有过接触的人。

paragraphs.en: PAK: This group, he says, generally trusts Huang's ability as the company's CEO and believes he would return, just not as fast as it happened, like 11 days.
paragraphs.zh: PAK：他说，这个团队通常信任黄作为公司首席执行官的能力，并且相信他会回来，只是不会像发生的那样快，比如11天。

paragraphs.en: SUMMERS: It was really fast, yeah. Now, what about the allegation that China launched a spy operation targeting NVIDIA and Huang? Has there been much discussion about that?
paragraphs.zh: 萨默斯：真的很快，是的。那么，关于中国发起针对英伟达和黄的间谍行动的指控呢？对此有很多讨论吗？

paragraphs.en: PAK: China's foreign ministry has denied these spy allegations. NPR has just heard that in the U.S., congressional staff have been briefed by American intelligence officials. And a person familiar with the matter said there is no evidence the woman who had an affair with NVIDIA chief Jensen Huang, named Alice Huang - of no relation - is a Chinese spy, though she is believed to have passed along information to the Chinese after the affair started.
paragraphs.zh: 巴基斯坦：中国外交部否认了这些间谍指控。NPR 刚获悉，在美国，国会工作人员已由美国情报官员进行了简报。一位知情人士表示，没有证据表明与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有婚外情的女性，名叫Alice Huang——与黄仁勋无亲属关系——是中国间谍，尽管据认为在婚外情开始后她曾向中国传递信息。

articles.title: How to talk AI around the Thanksgiving table
articles.dek: You're gathered with family this Thanksgiving when the topic of AI comes up. How can you have a productive, fact-based conversation?

paragraphs.en: You're gathered with family this Thanksgiving when the topic of AI comes up. How can you have a productive, fact-based conversation?
paragraphs.zh: 在这个感恩节，你和家人聚在一起时，话题转到了人工智能。你如何进行一次富有成效、基于事实的对话？

paragraphs.en: Thanksgiving dinner conversations can be fraught in some families. It is best to avoid certain topics, like politics or religion, and 2026 has given us a new land mine of small talk - AI. Machine Gods is here to help. Machine Gods is the new podcast from NPR about the AI future. In this excerpt, hosts Kevin Roose and Casey Newton offer some friendly advice for how to navigate AI dinner table talk.
paragraphs.zh: 在一些家庭中，感恩节晚餐的对话可能会充满紧张气氛。最好避免某些话题，例如政治或宗教，而2026年又为闲聊带来了新的雷区——人工智能。Machine Gods 来帮忙。Machine Gods 是 NPR 关于人工智能未来的新播客。在这段摘录中，主持人 Kevin Roose 和 Casey Newton 提供了一些友好的建议，教你如何应对围绕人工智能的餐桌话题。

paragraphs.en: CASEY NEWTON, BYLINE: Casey here with a quick disclosure at the top. As regular Machine Gods listeners know, my fiance works for Anthropic.
paragraphs.zh: 凯西·牛顿，署名：这里是凯西，先快速说明一下。如常听《机器之神》的听众所知，我的未婚夫在Anthropic工作。

paragraphs.en: ROOSE: ...We wanted to do something a little seasonal. We wanted to help our listeners with their Thanksgivings.
paragraphs.zh: ROOSE: ...我们想做一些应季的事情。我们想帮助我们的听众准备他们的感恩节。

paragraphs.en: NEWTON: Yes. You know, many podcasts will do advice around the holidays, and we got a question that it felt like we might actually be in a good position to answer.
paragraphs.zh: 牛顿：是的。你知道，许多播客会在假期期间提供建议，我们收到一个问题，感觉我们实际上可能处于一个可以回答的好位置。

paragraphs.en: ROOSE: So listener, Blythe (ph), wrote in to ask us, what are the three concise AI talking points you would have ready to share with your family at Thanksgiving, presumably, as we head into 2027? Let's first of all, start by examining the premise here.
paragraphs.zh: ROOSE：所以听众 Blythe（音）写信来问我们，你会准备哪三条简明的人工智能讨论要点，在感恩节与家人分享，大概是在我们迎接 2027 年的时候？让我们首先从审视这里的前提开始。

paragraphs.en: ROOSE: Is AI something you should be discussing with your family at Thanksgiving?
paragraphs.zh: 鲁斯：人工智能是你应该在感恩节与家人讨论的话题吗？

paragraphs.en: NEWTON: (Laughter) Listen, when it comes to discussing AI, I try to operate in a consent-based culture. So I am not out there just volunteering my opinions about AI to people. Now, it so happens that it will often come up in conversation. So I have given this some thought, and the first thing I would suggest you might want to tell your family, Kevin, is to try it. And what I mean by that is, have you actually sat down in front of ChatGPT recently and asked it to do something? And I say all of this not as an unrelenting promoter of the AI industry, but because it remains the best way I know how to wrap your brain around what is happening.
paragraphs.zh: 牛顿：（笑声）听着，当谈到人工智能时，我尽量在一种基于同意的文化中运作。所以我不会去随便向别人提供关于人工智能的意见。现在，碰巧的是，这通常会在对话中出现。所以我考虑过这个问题，我首先会建议你可能想告诉你的家人，凯文，是去尝试它。我的意思是，你最近是否真的坐在ChatGPT面前，让它去做某件事情？我说这些话不是作为人工智能行业的无条件推广者，而是因为它仍然是我所知道的理解正在发生的事情的最好方式。

paragraphs.en: ROOSE: Yes. That was my first piece of advice, too, is, like, show, don't tell.
paragraphs.zh: 鲁斯：是的。那也是我的第一个建议，就是，像是，展示，而不是讲述。

vocab.ex: You're gathered with family this Thanksgiving when the topic of AI comes up.
It is best to avoid certain topics, like politics or religion, and 2026 has given us a new land mine of small talk - AI.
Machine Gods is the new podcast from NPR about the AI future.
ROOSE: Is AI something you should be discussing with your family at Thanksgiving?
NEWTON: (Laughter) Listen, when it comes to discussing AI, I try to operate in a consent-based culture.
So I have given this some thought, and the first thing I would suggest you might want to tell your family, Kevin, is to try it.
And I say all of this not as an unrelenting promoter of the AI industry, but because it remains the best way I know how to wrap your brain around what is happening.

articles.title: A sweeping permitting reform bill is headed to the House. Critics want to stop it
articles.dek: President Trump supports a bipartisan bill that would speed up approval of federal infrastructure and energy projects. Critics say it will do so at the expense of the climate, tribes and public lands.

paragraphs.en: President Trump supports a bipartisan bill that would speed up approval of federal infrastructure and energy projects. Critics say it will do so at the expense of the climate, tribes and public lands.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普总统支持一项两党法案，该法案将加快联邦基础设施和能源项目的批准。批评人士称，这样做会以气候、部落和公共土地为代价。

paragraphs.en: With just weeks left in its term, Congress could reshape the country's physical landscape for generations. The Senate passed a bipartisan permitting reform bill that supporters say will pave the way for much needed infrastructure projects. But critics argue it will do so at the expense of the environment, tribes and public lands. They want the House to either fix or reject the bill before the year ends, as NPR's Rachel Treisman reports.
paragraphs.zh: 只剩下几个星期任期，国会可能会重塑国家的物理景观，影响几代人。参议院通过了一项两党共同支持的许可改革法案，支持者表示这将为急需的基础设施项目铺平道路。但批评者认为，这样做将以环境、部落和公共土地为代价。他们希望众议院在年底前要么修正这项法案，要么予以否决，正如NPR的Rachel Treisman报道的那样。

paragraphs.en: RACHEL TREISMAN, BYLINE: Last week, the Senate passed a bill that aims to speed up the approval process for federal infrastructure and energy projects, from wind turbines to data centers. It's called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA, and it's nearly 500 pages long.
paragraphs.zh: 雷切尔·特雷斯曼，署名：上周，参议院通过了一项法案，旨在加快联邦基础设施和能源项目的审批流程，从风力涡轮机到数据中心。它被称为《两党美国可负担性与就业法案》（BAAJA），长达近500页。

paragraphs.en: XAN FISHMAN: This isn't just, like, a mushy, middle, moderate, do-nothing bill. Like, it's actually a big-deal bill.
paragraphs.zh: XAN FISHMAN：这不仅仅是那种柔软、中庸、无所作为的法案。它实际上是一个重要的法案。

paragraphs.en: TREISMAN: Xan Fishman leads the energy program at the Bipartisan Policy Center.
paragraphs.zh: 特雷斯曼：扎恩·费什曼领导两党政策中心的能源项目。

paragraphs.en: FISHMAN: At its heart, it's about trying to take a permitting system which has just grown out of proportion and make sure that it's protecting the environment but getting to a yes or no answer in a reasonable amount of time.
paragraphs.zh: FISHMAN：归根结底，这关乎尝试将一个已经发展得失控的许可系统进行调整，确保它在保护环境的同时，也能在合理的时间内得出是或否的答案。

paragraphs.en: TREISMAN: Supporters of the bill say it will improve America's aging grid while creating jobs and lowering electricity bills. But critics say it would weaken bedrock environmental and historic preservation laws, including by limiting input from tribes and the public.
paragraphs.zh: 特里斯曼：该法案的支持者表示，它将改善美国老化的电网，同时创造就业机会并降低电费。但批评者则表示，它将削弱基础的环境和历史保护法律，包括通过限制部落和公众的意见。

paragraphs.en: WESLEY FURLONG: From our perspective, there are no pros. There are only cons.
paragraphs.zh: 韦斯利·富兰：从我们的角度来看，没有优点，只有缺点。

articles.title: A dish with a story, Thanksgiving with culinary historian Michael Twitty
articles.dek: Culinary historian Michael Twitty on tracing familial connections through food

paragraphs.en: Culinary historian Michael Twitty on tracing familial connections through food
paragraphs.zh: 美食历史学家迈克尔·特维通过食物追溯家庭联系

paragraphs.en: This Thanksgiving, Morning Edition host Leila Fadel left the studio for her kitchen, where she was met by the two-time James Beard Award winner Michael Twitty, who came with a spice blend, fresh sage, fish peppers and onions from his garden.
paragraphs.zh: 这个感恩节，《早间版》主持人莱拉·法德尔离开了演播室，走进她的厨房，在那里她遇到了两届詹姆斯·比尔德奖得主迈克尔·特维蒂，他带来了自己调制的香料、 свеж鼠尾草、鱼椒和他花园里的洋葱。

paragraphs.en: His book, The Cooking Gene, planted him as one of the nation's foremost chronologists tracing his ancestry through African American culinary history.
paragraphs.zh: 他的书《烹饪基因》使他成为全国最重要的编年史家之一，通过非裔美国人的烹饪历史追溯他的祖先。

paragraphs.en: Kush is one of Twitty's most beloved Thanksgiving offerings and one he's been making since he was a teen. The name and the ingredients show the way food became a tool for the enslaved in the Americas to preserve their cultures.
paragraphs.zh: Kush 是 Twitty 最受欢迎的感恩节美食之一，也是他从青少年时期就开始制作的菜肴。这个名字和食材展示了食物如何成为美洲被奴役者用来保存他们文化的工具。

paragraphs.en: "The name comes from Hausa, the language of West Africa. They are a predominantly Muslim people, but Muslim in the way that West Africans do Islam – which is Islam with a lot of the influence from the traditional culture and spirituality," he said on the origins of the side dish. "And so the name Kush, it's like, couscous," he added.
paragraphs.zh: 他说起这道配菜的起源时表示：“这个名字来自西非的语言豪萨语。他们是以穆斯林为主的民族，但他们的穆斯林信仰方式是西非人的方式——也就是说，他们的伊斯兰教融入了很多传统文化和灵性影响。”他补充道：“所以名字 Kush，就像是库斯库斯一样。”

paragraphs.en: "There was a time when I couldn't tell you what particular African ethnic groups I came from, but now that I know that I'm part Wolof, Hausa, Fula, and Serer and so many others," he said. "Now, I know this dish has a connection to who I am and my roots and where I came from."
paragraphs.zh: “曾经我无法告诉你我来自哪些特定的非洲族群，但现在我知道我部分是沃洛夫族、豪萨族、富拉族和瑟雷族以及许多其他族群，”他说。“现在，我知道这道菜与我是谁、我的根源以及我来自哪里有联系。”

paragraphs.en: In the making of this dish, Twitty also shared his work documenting the ways African American Jewish people create hybrid dishes in the kitchen.
paragraphs.zh: 在制作这道菜的过程中，特维蒂还分享了他记录非裔美国犹太人如何在厨房中制作混合菜肴的作品。

paragraphs.en: "It's Matzah ball gumbo, and it's black-eyed peas and quiche," he said of his Black and Jewish identity. "It's a lot of dishes that were from North Africa or from Ethiopia, it's kosher jollof rice and Shito. Shito usually has shellfish in it – we don't put that."
paragraphs.zh: “这是马扎球炖菜，还有黑眼豆和乳蛋饼，”他说到他的黑人和犹太身份时说。“有很多菜肴来自北非或埃塞俄比亚，是犹太洁食的焦洛夫米饭和Shito酱。Shito酱通常含有贝类——我们不放这个。”

articles.title: How American Thanksgiving took root -- and evolved -- in Liberia
articles.dek: How American Thanksgiving took root — and evolved — in Liberia

paragraphs.en: How American Thanksgiving took root — and evolved — in Liberia
paragraphs.zh: 美国感恩节如何在利比里亚生根——并发展

paragraphs.en: Yvonne Capehart Weah is from Liberia, a country in West Africa, and she's one of twelve siblings.
paragraphs.zh: 伊冯·凯普哈特·维亚来自利比里亚，这是西非的一个国家，她有十二个兄弟姐妹中的一个。

paragraphs.en: "I'm the second to the last one — I'm the eleventh," she says. "We have large families in Liberia."
paragraphs.zh: “我是倒数第二个——我是第十一位，”她说。“我们在利比里亚家庭都很大家庭。”

paragraphs.en: Every year on the first Thursday in November, Weah's family gathers in Caldwell, the township where she grew up, to celebrate Liberian Thanksgiving.
paragraphs.zh: 每年十一月的第一个星期四，维亚的家人都会在她成长的市镇考德威尔聚会，庆祝利比里亚感恩节。

paragraphs.en: "When we come together, the group become [so] large that you are not able to sit around a dining table," she explains. "So we do it outside under the tree. And when we meet, it's almost like we're having a party."
paragraphs.zh: “当我们聚在一起时，团队变得[如此]庞大，你无法围坐在餐桌旁，”她解释道。 “所以我们就在树下户外进行。当我们见面时，几乎就像是在开派对。”

paragraphs.en: The Liberian holiday dates back to the first half of the 19th century when the American Colonization Society established the community that would grow into the country. It was founded by Black Americans — both those born free and enslaved people who had been emancipated — whose departure was sometimes voluntary, sometimes forced. "The settlers from America brought that Thanksgiving Day tradition to Liberia," says Weah. Once transplanted, the holiday evolved over time in response to national events.
paragraphs.zh: 利比里亚的节日起源于19世纪上半叶，当时美国殖民协会建立了逐渐发展成为该国的社区。这个社区由黑人美国人创立——包括那些天生自由的人和已获解放的奴隶——他们的离开有时是自愿的，有时是被迫的。“来自美国的定居者将感恩节的传统带到了利比里亚，”韦亚说。一旦被引入，这个节日随着国家事件的发展逐渐演变。

paragraphs.en: Liberia gained its independence in 1847 but the British continued trying to take swaths of territory. In 1883, President Alfred Francis Russell, an Episcopalian priest, called upon God to help halt the incursions.
paragraphs.zh: 利比里亚在1847年获得独立，但英国人继续试图占领大片领土。1883年，主教会牧师、总统阿尔弗雷德·弗朗西斯·拉塞尔呼求上帝帮助阻止入侵。

paragraphs.en: That invocation was a "prayer of protection against the intruders, preventing intrusion into our territory," says Weah.
paragraphs.zh: 韦阿说：“那次祈祷是‘为防止入侵者进入我们的领土而进行的保护祈祷’。”

paragraphs.en: The Liberians managed to maintain their sovereignty. And that year, the legislature officially established Thanksgiving as a national holiday steeped in the religious gratitude of the moment.
paragraphs.zh: 利比里亚人设法保持了他们的主权。那一年，立法机构正式将感恩节确立为一个国家假日，充满了当时的宗教感恩情怀。

articles.title: U.S. Judge rules FCC violated ABC's free speech rights to please Trump
articles.dek: A federal judge has blocked President Trump and his administration from taking action to challenge the ABC television network's broadcast licenses, finding it to be an unconstitutional punishment…

paragraphs.en: A federal judge has blocked President Trump and his administration from taking action to challenge the ABC television network's broadcast licenses, finding it to be an unconstitutional punishment for satire, commentary and news coverage that Trump doesn't like.
paragraphs.zh: 一名联邦法官已阻止特朗普总统及其政府采取行动挑战ABC电视网的广播许可证，裁定这是对特朗普不喜欢的讽刺、评论和新闻报道的违宪惩罚。

paragraphs.en: In her preliminary injunction filed Wednesday, U.S. District Court Judge Loren AliKhan found that the federal agency's early reviews represented retaliation for speech the Trump administration resented.
paragraphs.zh: 在她于周三提交的初步禁令中，美国地方法院法官洛伦·阿里汗认定，该联邦机构的早期审查是对特朗普政府不满的言论的报复。

paragraphs.en: Such perceived offenses included late-night host Jimmy Kimmel's jabs at the president, the critical remarks of hosts on the chat show The View, and the moderation of a presidential debate in September 2024.
paragraphs.zh: 这种被认为的冒犯包括深夜节目主持人吉米·基梅尔对总统的嘲讽、《观点》访谈节目主持人的批评性言论，以及2024年9月的一场总统辩论的主持方式。

paragraphs.en: ABC and its corporate parent, the Walt Disney Co., serve six of the 10 largest markets in the U.S., including New York, Los Angeles, and Houston. They contribute significantly to the network's bottom line.
paragraphs.zh: ABC及其母公司沃尔特·迪士尼公司在美国最大的十个市场中服务于六个市场，包括纽约、洛杉矶和休斯顿。他们对该网络的盈利贡献显著。

paragraphs.en: "Given the extreme, indeed existential, nature of the possible penalty Plaintiffs face -- loss of their broadcast licenses -- the court concludes that early license renewal proceedings create a risk sufficient to chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness," Judge AliKhan wrote.
paragraphs.zh: 阿里汗法官写道：“鉴于原告可能面临的处罚具有极端性，甚至关系生死——失去他们的广播许可——法院认为，提前的许可证续期程序造成的风险足以使一名普通坚韧的广播员感到畏缩。”

paragraphs.en: She rejected the Trump administration's motion to dismiss the lawsuit from ABC and Disney challenging the review of the local licenses. Usually the licenses last eight years and are up for review on a staggered basis. They are rarely taken away.
paragraphs.zh: 她驳回了特朗普政府要求驳回ABC和迪士尼针对地方牌照审查的诉讼的动议。通常，这些牌照有效期为八年，并且是分批进行审查的。它们很少被收回。

paragraphs.en: In her ruling, AliKhan relied heavily on public statements and social media postings in which Trump attacked ABC and Disney, as well as posts by Trump's pick as the chair of the Federal Communications Commission, Brendan Carr.
paragraphs.zh: 在她的裁决中，阿里汗主要依赖特朗普攻击ABC和迪士尼的公开声明和社交媒体帖子，以及特朗普提名的联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹·卡尔的帖子。

paragraphs.en: "What started in 2020 as questions about how ABC 'can keep getting a license' if it 'report[s] fake news,' ... has crescendoed into repeated calls for the Commission to strip ABC's broadcast licenses for their editorial decisions," she wrote. "The court counts eleven such calls made by President Trump over the past two years -- the most recent being in July 2026."
paragraphs.zh: 她写道：“从2020年开始，人们就开始质疑ABC‘如何在报导假新闻的情况下仍能获得许可’，……这已经升级为反复要求委员会因ABC的编辑决策而剥夺其广播许可证的呼声。” “法院统计了特朗普总统在过去两年中提出的十一次此类呼吁——最近的一次是在2026年7月。”

articles.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
articles.dek: The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company,…

paragraphs.en: The Trump administration on Wednesday gave SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a long-lofty goal of Elon Musk's rocket company, in a move that has raised both skepticism and alarm among some scientists.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普政府周三批准了SpaceX部署100万颗卫星，该公司表示这些卫星将创建太空数据中心，这是埃隆·马斯克的火箭公司的一个长期远大目标，此举引发了一些科学家的怀疑和警觉。

paragraphs.en: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission lauded its authorization as a historic first amid the artificial intelligence race. It said that SpaceX's one million "orbital compute modules" (forming a data center constellation called "Starmind") would process massive amounts of data that would be used back on Earth — and bring humans closer to harnessing "the full power of the sun."
paragraphs.zh: 美国联邦通信委员会称其批准为人工智能竞赛中的历史性首次。委员会表示，SpaceX 的一百万个“轨道计算模块”（形成一个名为“Starmind”的数据中心星座）将处理大量数据，这些数据将用于地球上的应用——并使人类更接近利用“太阳的全部力量”。

paragraphs.en: "America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, who was appointed by Republican President Donald Trump, said in a statement. He added that Wednesday's move "opens a bold new frontier."
paragraphs.zh: “美国正在引领世界进入超级智能时代，”由共和党总统唐纳德·特朗普任命的FCC主席布伦丹·卡尔在一份声明中表示。他补充说，周三的举措“开启了一个大胆的新前沿。”

paragraphs.en: A lengthier authorization order published by the FCC noted that the company must deploy at least "one authorized space station" by 2033 — and then gradually add more and more through 2040. Musk welcomed the decision over social media.
paragraphs.zh: 美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）发布的一份较长的授权命令指出，该公司必须在2033年前部署至少“一颗获授权的卫星”，然后在2040年前逐步增加更多。马斯克在社交媒体上对这一决定表示欢迎。

paragraphs.en: The world's richest man has long vowed to form vast, solar-powered data centers in space to help run AI tools on Earth. But scientists and industry experts have stressed enormous technical and financial obstacles, as well as a host of environmental concerns.
paragraphs.zh: 世界首富长期以来一直誓言在太空建立庞大的太阳能数据中心，以帮助在地球上运行人工智能工具。但科学家和行业专家强调了巨大的技术和财务障碍，以及一系列环境问题。

paragraphs.en: Adam Becker, an astrophysicist and author, called the prospect of launching a million satellites into space to create data centers "a fantasy."
paragraphs.zh: 天体物理学家兼作家亚当·贝克称将一百万颗卫星发射到太空以建立数据中心的前景为“一种幻想”。

paragraphs.en: Proponents of data centers in space argue that capturing the sun's energy would ease pressure on power grids and cut demand for sprawling computing warehouses on Earth (and resources like water needed to cool them). Space seems to offer a solution because it is cold, but it is also a vacuum, trapping heat inside objects much like a thermos. Becker explained that there are "basic physical limits" to otherwise radiating that heat out — and sending lots of smaller satellites could potentially carry the necessary material combined, but it would be expensive and difficult.
paragraphs.zh: 空间数据中心的支持者认为，捕获太阳能可以减轻电网的压力，并减少对地面大型计算仓库以及用于冷却它们的水等资源的需求。空间似乎提供了一种解决方案，因为那里很冷，但它也是一个真空，就像保温瓶一样将热量困在物体内部。Becker解释说，要将热量辐射出去存在“基本的物理限制”——而发送大量较小的卫星可能可以组合携带所需材料，但这将既昂贵又困难。

paragraphs.en: He and others also point to additional risks, such as atmospheric pollution through launches and reentries, as well as possible in-orbit collisions that could impact other essential satellites.
paragraphs.zh: 他和其他人还指出了额外的风险，例如发射和再入大气层导致的大气污染，以及可能发生的轨道内碰撞，这些碰撞可能影响其他重要的卫星。

articles.title: These deer walk 300 miles a year. The race is on to save their migration
articles.dek: On a spring morning, a mule deer and her fawn follow a well-worn trail through the Wyoming sagebrush. They're on a 150-mile journey, one of the longest land migrations in the lower 48 states.

paragraphs.en: On a spring morning, a mule deer and her fawn follow a well-worn trail through the Wyoming sagebrush. They're on a 150-mile journey, one of the longest land migrations in the lower 48 states.
paragraphs.zh: 在一个春天的早晨，一只骡鹿和她的幼鹿沿着怀俄明州鼠尾草丛中的一条常走的小径行进。它们正在进行一次150英里的旅程，这是美国本土48州中最长的陆地迁徙之一。

paragraphs.en: Like many other migrations in the U.S., the mule deer's epic journey is hidden in plain sight. Mule deer move in small groups instead of large herds, following pathways likely used for millennia. They're part of the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem in western Wyoming, a place where elk, deer and pronghorn antelope still have the space to move across vast landscapes.
paragraphs.zh: 像美国的许多其他迁徙一样，骡鹿的史诗般旅程隐藏在显眼之处。骡鹿以小群体而不是大群体移动，沿着可能已使用千年的路径行进。它们是怀俄明州西部大黄石生态系统的一部分，在那里，麋鹿、鹿和叉角羚羚仍然有空间在广阔的土地上迁徙。

paragraphs.en: They migrate with careful seasonal choreography, timed to reach the best feeding grounds in summer and avoid the harshest winter weather. Still, as the climate gets hotter, that timing is being tested.
paragraphs.zh: 它们按着精心安排的季节性节奏迁徙，时机掌握在夏季到达最佳觅食地，并躲避最严酷的冬季天气。然而，随着气候变得更热，这种时机正在受到考验。

paragraphs.en: Droughts are getting more intense in the Western U.S., limiting the food supplies for deer. Their migrations are also being constricted by development, forcing them to navigate a complex maze of fences, roads and subdivisions. Research shows mule deer may be able to adapt to increasingly unpredictable seasons, but development is limiting that ability.
paragraphs.zh: 美国西部的干旱越来越严重，限制了鹿的食物供应。它们的迁徙也受到开发的限制，迫使它们穿越复杂的围栏、道路和住宅区迷宫。研究表明，骡鹿可能能够适应越来越不可预测的季节，但开发正在限制这一能力。

paragraphs.en: Wyoming is working to keep migration routes from being severed. It's one of the few states that has protected migratory corridors for wildlife, restricting development in the most crucial paths. Landowners and conservation groups are also permanently preserving open lands and working ranches.
paragraphs.zh: 怀俄明州正在努力防止迁徙路线被切断。它是为数不多的几个为野生动物保护迁徙通道的州之一，在最关键的路径上限制开发。土地所有者和保护组织也在永久保护开放土地和运作中的农场。

paragraphs.en: The question is whether that work can keep pace with growth. Wyoming's migratory wildlife are on the decline. The state's mule deer population was more than 500,000 in 1990. It's now half of that number.
paragraphs.zh: 问题是那项工作是否能跟上增长的步伐。怀俄明州的候鸟野生动物数量正在下降。1990 年，该州的骡鹿数量超过 50 万。现在只剩一半。

paragraphs.en: "The history of wildlife migration is one of loss – we've lost migrations around the world," says Matt Kauffman, wildlife biologist with the U.S. Geological Survey and the University of Wyoming. "We are in this little race to map the migrations and figure out what tools we need to keep those landscapes open, as the American West continues to change."
paragraphs.zh: “野生动物迁徙的历史是一个失落的历史——我们已经在世界各地失去了迁徙，”美国地质调查局和怀俄明大学的野生动物生物学家马特·考夫曼说。“我们正处在这场小小的竞赛中，试图绘制迁徙路线图，并弄清楚我们需要什么工具来保持这些景观的开放，因为美国西部正在不断变化。”

paragraphs.en: In the foothills outside Pinedale, Wyoming, Kauffman and research associate Ashley Townsend make their way through the sagebrush, scanning for a radio signal. They pick one up – a beep, beep, beep – from a mule deer with a tracking collar, which the team put on months earlier.
paragraphs.zh: 在怀俄明州派恩代尔外的山麓地带，考夫曼和研究助理阿什利·汤森穿过鼠尾草丛，搜索无线电信号。他们接收到一个信号——哔、哔、哔——来自一只戴着跟踪项圈的骡鹿，这是团队几个月前给它戴上的。

paragraphs.en: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" and were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.
paragraphs.zh: 安迪·泰勒，1980年代英国新浪潮乐队Duran Duran的原吉他手，该乐队的巨大流行曲目包括《Hungry Like the Wolf》《The Reflex》和《Rio》，并与MTV的启动密不可分，已去世。他享年65岁。

paragraphs.en: Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.
paragraphs.zh: 泰勒的死亡得到了他的家人和乐队成员的确认，他们在社交媒体和杜兰杜兰乐队的网站上发布了声明。

paragraphs.en: "From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed," the band said.
paragraphs.zh: 乐队表示：“从他从东北带着吉他和对我们未来可能成就的坚定信念抵达伯明翰的那一刻起，他就为我们的音乐带来了不可磨灭的激情和自信。他的演奏推动了那些带我们走遍世界的歌曲，而他那干练的机智，以及他那极其实际、毫不矫情的人生态度，让我们保持脚踏实地，并在接下来的非凡岁月中赋予乐队锋芒。”

paragraphs.en: On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.
paragraphs.zh: 2022年11月，在他入选摇滚名人堂的那个晚上，泰勒透露他已经与四期转移性前列腺癌抗争了数年，因此无法出席。

paragraphs.en: "I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."
paragraphs.zh: 他写道：“我想感谢这个伟大乐队中的每一位兄弟。你可以梦想我们所经历的事情，但亲身体验它，以自己的方式，作为伙伴，那真是难以置信。”

paragraphs.en: The two-time Grammy Award-winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.
paragraphs.zh: 这两次格莱美奖得主拥有九张金唱片和六张白金唱片，在英国有20首进入前20名的单曲，在美国有18首。他们是两次艾沃·诺维洛奖得主，也是MTV视频先锋奖的获得者。

paragraphs.en: The band's 1981 debut album "Duran Duran" had their first hit single, "Planet Earth," but it was "Rio" that transformed them into trans-Atlantic stars. The Rock Hall explained their appeal this way: "They were new wave outsiders who became music video stars — 'Tiger Beat' fashion pinups who rocked arenas."
paragraphs.zh: 该乐队1981年的首张专辑《Duran Duran》推出了他们的第一首热门单曲《Planet Earth》，但正是《Rio》让他们成为跨大西洋的明星。摇滚名人堂这样解释他们的吸引力：“他们是成为音乐视频明星的新潮外来者——《Tiger Beat》时尚偶像，在大型体育馆演出。”

paragraphs.en: The band's imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as "Girls on Film" and "Union of the Snake" and the moody ballads "The Chauffeur" and "Save a Prayer." Other hits in the coming years included "The Wild Boys," "New Moon on Monday" and "Come Undone." Their popularity was cemented when they recorded the James Bond theme song "A View to a Kill" and earned a slot at Live Aid in 1985.
paragraphs.zh: 乐队的巅峰时期发生在1981年至1983年之间，他们推出了三张热门专辑，其中包括舞池热曲《Girls on Film》和《Union of the Snake》，以及情绪化的抒情歌《The Chauffeur》和《Save a Prayer》。在接下来的几年里，其他热门歌曲还包括《The Wild Boys》、《New Moon on Monday》和《Come Undone》。他们的人气在录制詹姆斯·邦德主题曲《A View to a Kill》并获得1985年Live Aid演出机会时得到了巩固。

articles.title: Who really owns the Albanian land Jared Kushner wants to turn into a 5-star resort?
articles.dek: ZVERNEC, Albania — In the summer of 2021, Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump boarded a yacht owned by Nat Rothschild, an heir to the European banking family. On the way from Montenegro to Greece, the…

paragraphs.en: ZVERNEC, Albania — In the summer of 2021, Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump boarded a yacht owned by Nat Rothschild, an heir to the European banking family. On the way from Montenegro to Greece, the yacht anchored off the coast of Albania.
paragraphs.zh: 阿尔巴尼亚兹韦尔内茨 — 2021年夏天，贾里德·库什纳和伊万卡·特朗普登上了由纳特·罗斯柴尔德拥有的游艇，他是欧洲银行世家的继承人。在从黑山到希腊的途中，游艇在阿尔巴尼亚海岸停泊。

paragraphs.en: And, as Kushner told an investment conference last year, that's when Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama arrived at the boat to tell them about his plan for the country.
paragraphs.zh: 正如库什纳去年在一次投资会议上所说的，那时阿尔巴尼亚总理埃迪·拉马来到船上，向他们讲述他对国家的计划。

paragraphs.en: "I was very impressed by what he wanted to do with the country," said Kushner. "I really didn't know anything about the country and I didn't understand the history, and the darkness of the history with the communism and terrible leadership led to it being fully undeveloped as a nation."
paragraphs.zh: 库什纳说：“我对他想要对这个国家所做的事情印象非常深刻。我真的对这个国家一无所知，也不了解历史，而共产主义和可怕领导下的历史黑暗导致它作为一个国家完全未开发。”

paragraphs.en: A year later, Kushner was looking for development opportunities in the Balkans. He returned to the Albanian coast — to the city of Vlore, which was finishing the construction of an airport atop a wetland near an undeveloped coastline. "And obviously, a country's going to build an airport by the coast in a place they think is most beautiful," Kushner told the conference, "so we went there and we were looking for opportunities, and we found some incredible opportunities."
paragraphs.zh: 一年后，库什纳正在寻找在巴尔干地区的发展机会。他回到了阿尔巴尼亚海岸——弗洛雷市，那里的湿地靠近一片未开发的海岸线，机场建设即将完工。“显然，一个国家会在他们认为最美的地方沿海建机场，”库什纳在会议上说，“所以我们去了那里，寻找机会，并且我们发现了一些令人难以置信的机会。”

paragraphs.en: Kushner found those opportunities at Hidrovor Beach, an expanse of caramel-colored sand along the southern Albanian coast, with the gentle waves of the Adriatic lapping its perimeter and a view of an uninhabited island. A company working for Kushner purchased this land and 300 acres surrounding it for more than $130 million in April. But several people here tell NPR this is not Kushner's land.
paragraphs.zh: 库什纳在Hidrovor海滩发现了这些机会，这里是阿尔巴尼亚南部海岸上一片焦糖色的沙滩，亚得里亚海的温和海浪拍打着海滩边缘，可以看到一座无人居住的岛屿。一家为库什纳工作的公司在四月以超过1.3亿美元的价格购买了这块土地及其周围的300英亩土地。但这里的几个人告诉NPR，这并不是库什纳的土地。

paragraphs.en: "This land here belonged to my family for centuries," says Gentian Mocka, who claims his family has owned this strip of beach and wetland since the time of the Ottoman Empire. He provided NPR land titles that appear to prove this.
paragraphs.zh: “这片土地属于我的家族已经数百年了，”Gentian Mocka说道，他声称他的家族自奥斯曼帝国时期起就拥有这片海滩和湿地。他向NPR提供了似乎可以证明这一点的土地所有权文件。

paragraphs.en: After World War II, Albania's Communist government seized it — along with all private land.
paragraphs.zh: 二战后，阿尔巴尼亚的共产党政府没收了它——以及所有私人土地。

paragraphs.en: When communism fell in 1991, families like Mocka's embarked on a years-long process to get their land back. "But then our problems started with the guys that were much more powerful than we were — had a lot of political support, were very rich and very well connected with the politics of that time," says Mocka.
paragraphs.zh: 当共产主义在1991年垮台时，像莫卡这样的家庭开始了长达数年的土地取回过程。莫卡说：“但之后我们的问题开始出现在那些比我们强大得多的人身上——他们拥有大量政治支持，非常富有，并且与当时的政治关系密切。”

articles.title: Unpacking President Trump's financial stake in Nvidia
articles.dek: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Dan Alexander, a senior editor at Forbes and author of a book about President Trump's businesses, about the president's holdings in Nvidia given recent news.

paragraphs.en: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Dan Alexander, a senior editor at Forbes and author of a book about President Trump's businesses, about the president's holdings in Nvidia given recent news.
paragraphs.zh: NPR的Scott Detrow与福布斯高级编辑、《总统特朗普商业》一书的作者Dan Alexander讨论了关于总统在Nvidia持股的最新消息。

paragraphs.en: Let's connect a few things we know about this whole Nvidia situation. One is that President Trump said he convinced Nvidia's board of directors to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Another is that Trump, or the people who manage his money, have purchased a lot of Nvidia stock since this second term began. One more thing to consider. Nvidia's stock price has roughly tripled over the past three years during the AI investment boom and as Jensen Huang has become a trusted advisor to the Trump White House. So how should we think about all this? We're going to bring in Dan Alexander, a senior editor at Forbes, who oversees coverage of money and politics. He's also an MS NOW contributor. Thanks for coming by.
paragraphs.zh: 让我们把关于整个英伟达情况的一些已知信息联系起来。首先，特朗普总统表示他说服了英伟达的董事会，让黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官。其次，特朗普或管理他资金的人，自他第二任期开始以来购买了大量英伟达股票。还有一件事要考虑。过去三年，在人工智能投资热潮期间，随着黄仁勋成为特朗普白宫的可信顾问，英伟达的股价大约翻了三倍。那么，我们该如何看待这一切呢？我们将请来《福布斯》的高级编辑丹·亚历山大，他负责监督财务和政治报道。他还是MS NOW的撰稿人。感谢您的到来。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: Is there a number or a stat that you can cite that best represents President Trump's holdings in Nvidia?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：有没有一个数字或统计数据可以代表特朗普总统在英伟达的持股情况？

paragraphs.en: ALEXANDER: But the latest reporting suggests that the range of his holdings is roughly 5 to $54 million. The stock price is moving a lot each year day.
paragraphs.zh: 亚历山大：但最新的报道显示，他的持股范围大约在 5 到 5400 万美元之间。股票价格每天波动很大。

paragraphs.en: ALEXANDER: So that's a number that is big, but also undetermined. And keep in mind that Trump's overall liquid holdings are roughly $2 billion.
paragraphs.zh: 亚历山大：所以这是一个很大的数字，但也是不确定的。记住，特朗普的总体流动资产大约为20亿美元。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: So this is a large amount of money, incredible wealth for most people. But in the scheme of Donald Trump's holdings, not the biggest asset.
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：所以这是一大笔钱，对于大多数人来说是难以置信的财富。但在唐纳德·特朗普的财产中，这并不是最大的资产。

paragraphs.en: ALEXANDER: Not the biggest asset by a long shot. But that doesn't necessarily mean that he doesn't think about the fact that it's an asset.
paragraphs.zh: 亚历山大：绝对算不上最大的资产。但这并不一定意味着他不考虑它是一个资产这个事实。

paragraphs.en: ALEXANDER: And particularly if it's on the higher end of that range, I mean, you know, $50 million certainly matters to Donald Trump.
paragraphs.zh: 亚历山大：特别是如果它在那个范围的高端，我是说，你知道，5000万美元对唐纳德·特朗普来说肯定很重要。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: Yeah. I mean, the range that you're giving comes from financial disclosures, right?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：是的。我是说，你给出的范围是来自财务披露，对吧？

articles.title: How high technology is changing cargo crime
articles.dek: Now our Planet Money podcast brings us a tale of highway bandits and holiday turkeys. Sarah Gonzalez reports that an age-old crime of hijacking is blending with high technology.

paragraphs.en: Now our Planet Money podcast brings us a tale of highway bandits and holiday turkeys. Sarah Gonzalez reports that an age-old crime of hijacking is blending with high technology.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，我们的《Planet Money》播客为我们带来了一个关于公路强盗和节日火鸡的故事。Sarah Gonzalez 报道说，一种古老的劫夺犯罪正在与高科技结合。

paragraphs.en: SARAH GONZALEZ, BYLINE: What was the load? What did they steal?
paragraphs.zh: 萨拉·冈萨雷斯，署名：装载的是什么？他们偷了什么？

paragraphs.en: JOHN: A hundred and two thousand dollars is what that one was.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰：那一个是十万二千美元。

paragraphs.en: GONZALEZ: John (ph) owns a line of trucks that have been targeted and hit twice now. Food and beverage cargo theft, in particular, is up 47%. It's hard to trace a missing turkey, you know? And cargo theft does get a little predictable around the holidays.
paragraphs.zh: 冈萨雷斯：约翰（音）拥有一条卡车线路，现在已经两次成为目标并受到攻击。特别是食品和饮料货物的盗窃，增加了47%。追踪一只丢失的火鸡很难，你知道吗？而且在假期期间，货物盗窃确实变得有些可预测。

paragraphs.en: GONZALEZ: Just a couple weeks ago, $10,000 worth of beef was stolen. A tequila truck's been hit. Half a million dollars' worth of shellfish was hijacked. In June, Rob Cook with the company A21 Wine & Spirits, lost half a million dollars' worth of bourbon.
paragraphs.zh: 冈萨雷斯：就在几周前，价值一万美元的牛肉被盗。一辆龙舌兰酒卡车遭到袭击。价值五十万美元的贝类被劫持。六月，公司A21葡萄酒与烈酒的Rob Cook损失了价值五十万美元的波本威士忌。

paragraphs.en: ROB COOK: Yeah, it was a full truck load of Noble Oak bourbon.
paragraphs.zh: 罗布·库克：是的，那是一整卡车的诺布尔橡木波本威士忌。

paragraphs.en: GONZALEZ: All right, here's how these schemes work. Hackers are targeting the nerve center of the trucking industry, their load boards. Load boards are like these online bulletin boards where a company like Rob's will say, hey, I have a load I need picked up in Philly and sent to New Jersey. And then certified truck drivers go on and say, I want that job. I'll move that load. Rob's bourbon was matched with the trucker on these load boards. The bourbon was picked up, but then never arrived. They called the dispatcher to check in, a guy named Eddie (ph).
paragraphs.zh: 冈萨雷斯：好吧，这些骗局是这样运作的。黑客瞄准了卡车运输行业的神经中枢——他们的货运板。货运板就像这些在线公告板，公司像Rob's会在上面发布信息，说，嘿，我有一批货物需要从费城运到新泽西。然后认证的卡车司机会上去说，我想接这个工作，我来运这批货。Rob's的波本威士忌就是通过这些货运板与卡车司机匹配的。波本威士忌被取走了，但却从未送到。他们给调度员打电话去确认，一个叫埃迪的人。

paragraphs.en: COOK: Eddie, hey, where's our load? It hasn't shown up yet. Eddie says, oh, it'll be there in an hour.
paragraphs.zh: 厨师：埃迪，嘿，我们的货物在哪儿？还没到。埃迪说，哦，一小时后会到的。

articles.title: Oil slicks in the Strait of Hormuz are harming the environment
articles.dek: More than 600 oil slicks threaten marine life in the Strait of Hormuz as war and tanker attacks turn vital waters into an environmental disaster.

paragraphs.en: More than 600 oil slicks threaten marine life in the Strait of Hormuz as war and tanker attacks turn vital waters into an environmental disaster.
paragraphs.zh: 随着战争和油轮袭击将关键水域变成环境灾难，霍尔木兹海峡有超过600处油污威胁海洋生物。

paragraphs.en: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps has been attacking oil tankers at a record pace. The IRGC says it's hitting several tankers a day. That's despite U.S. military efforts to guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz. NPR's Aya Batrawy saw oil washing ashore in the nearby United Arab Emirates.
paragraphs.zh: 伊朗革命卫队以创纪录的速度袭击油轮。伊朗革命卫队表示每天攻击数艘油轮。尽管美国军方努力引导船只通过霍尔木兹海峡，但袭击仍在发生。NPR的阿娅·巴特拉维看到石油冲上海滩，在附近的阿拉伯联合酋长国。

paragraphs.en: AYA BATRAWY, BYLINE: It's a bright and sunny day here in Khor Fakkan in the United Arab Emirates. And this beach is open, there's families here, the water is clear. But there are several stretches of the beach in the United Arab Emirates that are now closed because of oil spills because Iran continues to attack oil tankers trying to go in or out of the Strait of Hormuz.
paragraphs.zh: 阿雅·巴特劳伊，署名：这里是阿拉伯联合酋长国的霍尔法坎，今天阳光明媚。这个海滩开放，很多家庭在这里，水很清澈。但阿联酋有几段海滩现在关闭，因为发生了石油泄漏，而伊朗继续攻击试图进出霍尔木兹海峡的油轮。

paragraphs.en: BATRAWY: The U.N. has tracked around 150 attacks on ships since the start of the war. Greenpeace says its satellite monitoring has identified more than 600 possible oil slicks across Gulf waters from these attacks and the war, stretching some 8,000 square miles. Inesaf Benzaki is a campaigner with Greenpeace Middle East and North Africa.
paragraphs.zh: BATRAWY：联合国自战争开始以来已经追踪了大约150起针对船只的袭击。绿色和平组织表示，其卫星监测已经发现这些袭击和战争可能在海湾水域产生了超过600处油污，面积约为8,000平方英里。Inesaf Benzaki 是绿色和平中东和北非地区的活动家。

paragraphs.en: INESAF BENZAKI: It is really the repeated aspect of it in such a small area that compounds the scale of the damage. And yes, of course long-term monitoring, environmental monitoring is essential. But we can gauge that recovery will need a lot of time.
paragraphs.zh: 伊内萨夫·本扎基：真正加剧损害规模的是它在如此小的区域内反复发生的特点。当然，长期监测、环境监测是必不可少的。但我们可以判断，恢复将需要很长时间。

paragraphs.en: BATRAWY: She says the damage from these repeated oil spills is not only harming marine life and sensitive ecosystems like mangroves, but also the food chain and drinking water supplies the Gulf relies on. One of Iran's attacks on October 2 struck a ship carrying 2 million barrels of crude. That oil washed up on the UAE's shores a couple weeks later. The entire coast of the emirate of Umm Al Quwain has been closed to the public ever since. The sand has dark brown hues, and the smell of oil permeates the air.
paragraphs.zh: BATRAWY：她说，这些反复发生的石油泄漏造成的损害不仅危害海洋生物和像红树林这样的敏感生态系统，还影响海湾依赖的食物链和饮用水供应。伊朗在10月2日的一次袭击击中了运载200万桶原油的一艘船。几周后，这些原油漂到了阿联酋的海岸。自此之后，乌姆盖万酋长国的整个海岸对公众关闭。沙滩呈深棕色，空气中弥漫着石油的气味。

paragraphs.en: I can see a clean-up crew. I can see men in, you know, these hazard outfits cleaning up the coast. There's some kind of generator running and a hose to sort of suck, I guess, the oil, the petrol out of the water.
paragraphs.zh: 我可以看到一个清理队。我可以看到一些穿着危险防护服的人在清理海岸。那里有某种发电机在运转，还有一根管子，好像是用来吸出海水中的油和汽油。

paragraphs.en: To draw attention to the environmental costs of the war, British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh swam in the Strait of Hormuz this month. Pugh describes the experience for The Associated Press.
paragraphs.zh: 为了引起人们对战争环境成本的关注，英国耐力游泳运动员刘易斯·普格本月在霍尔木兹海峡游泳。普格向美联社描述了这一经历。

articles.title: How tariffs, fuel and fertilizer costs are squeezing the U.S.'s biggest apple region
articles.dek: As Sean Gilbert stepped out of his white GMC pickup, he breathed in the scent of applewood and Columbia Basin dust. Here, just south of Wapato, Wash., one of his 50-acre Gala and Red Delicious…

paragraphs.en: As Sean Gilbert stepped out of his white GMC pickup, he breathed in the scent of applewood and Columbia Basin dust. Here, just south of Wapato, Wash., one of his 50-acre Gala and Red Delicious apple orchards is ground into huge piles of mulch chips. The wood chipper is the size of a semi-truck and belts out a screeching racket.
paragraphs.zh: 当肖恩·吉尔伯特走出他那辆白色的GMC皮卡时，他吸入了苹果木和哥伦比亚盆地尘土的气息。在这里，位于华盛顿州瓦帕托以南，他的50英亩嘎啦苹果和红美味苹果果园之一被碾成了巨大的覆盖物木屑堆。木屑机的大小相当于一辆半挂卡车，发出尖锐刺耳的噪音。

paragraphs.en: He said this ground will lay fallow. It will cost this fifth-generation apple farmer less to leave it unplanted and weedy than to plant another orchard or crop. He scooped up a handful of applewood mulch. "It's a bit of a relief that we're not going to continue to be hemorrhaging dollars on orchards that the market doesn't want," he said. "It hasn't been making sense for a while."
paragraphs.zh: 他说这块地将闲置不耕种。对于这位已经传承到第五代的苹果农来说，不种植、任其长满杂草的成本比再种一个果园或农作物要低。他捧起一把苹果木覆盖物，说：“我们不再在市场不需要的果园上不断亏钱，有点松了一口气。”他说，“这已经有一阵子不合算了。”

paragraphs.en: Washington's $9 billion industry grows nearly 70% of the nation's fresh apples, according to Jon DeVaney, president of the Washington State Tree Fruit Association.
paragraphs.zh: 根据华盛顿州果树协会主席乔恩·德瓦尼的说法，华盛顿州价值90亿美元的产业生产了全国近70%的鲜苹果。

paragraphs.en: DeVaney said farmers are being pressed by the costs of labor, fuel, fertilizer, equipment, as well as weak exports from international tariffs and a strong dollar that diminishes foreign purchasing power.
paragraphs.zh: DeVaney表示，农民正受到劳动力、燃料、化肥、设备成本的压力，以及由于国际关税和强势美元削弱了外国购买力而导致的出口疲软的影响。

paragraphs.en: He estimated thousands of acres of apple orchards across the Northwest are being rapidly torn out, or are not being actively cared for, because many farmers aren't making money growing the fruit. And after several years of similar economic conditions, many farms have gone deep into debt – with even some large, well-established operations filing for bankruptcy.
paragraphs.zh: 他估计，整个西北部的数千英亩苹果园正在迅速被拆除，或者没有得到积极管理，因为许多农民种植苹果无法赚钱。在经历了几年类似的经济状况之后，许多农场已经陷入巨额债务——甚至一些大型、知名的经营实体也不得不申请破产。

paragraphs.en: In the late summer and fall, unpicked apples have been left to rot in branches and on the ground. Over the past few years, an estimated thousands of acres have only been partially picked or not picked at all, according to Kate Tynan, senior vice president of the Northwest Horticultural Council, a trade association that advocates for the Northwest tree fruit industry on federal policy issues and international trade.
paragraphs.zh: 在晚夏和秋季，未采摘的苹果被遗留在树枝上和地面上腐烂。根据西北园艺委员会高级副总裁凯特·泰南（Kate Tynan）的说法，过去几年，据估计有数千英亩的苹果园只是部分采摘或根本没有采摘。该委员会是一个贸易协会，代表西北地区的果树产业在联邦政策问题和国际贸易上进行倡导。

paragraphs.en: Recent federal regulatory changes would effectively lower wages for some immigrant workers and take housing costs out of their paychecks. Tynan said with updates to the way wages are calculated, farm owners are hoping they'll be able to break even – but the farm workers union has pushed back on these changes and an upcoming federal judicial decision could put operators on the hook for backpay for the 2026 season.
paragraphs.zh: 近期的联邦监管变动实际上会降低一些移民工人的工资，并将住房成本从他们的工资中剔除。泰南表示，随着工资计算方式的更新，农场主希望他们能够保本——但农场工人工会对这些变动提出了反对意见，而即将到来的联邦司法裁决可能会让经营者为2026年的工作季支付补发工资负责。

paragraphs.en: U.S. farmers have also been especially hard hit by tariffs and high input costs. The Trump administration announced $12 billion in payments to farmers at the end of 2025 that primarily targeted farmers who grow crops such as soybeans and corn. Tynan said much of that relief has not reached farmers that grow specialty crops like fruit and vegetables.
paragraphs.zh: 美国农民也因关税和高投入成本而受到特别严重的打击。特朗普政府在2025年底宣布向农民提供120亿美元的支付，这些支付主要针对种植大豆和玉米等作物的农民。泰南表示，这些救济金中的大部分尚未到达种植水果和蔬菜等特种作物的农民手中。

articles.title: Bleeding, birth defects: Congo residents sue over alleged mining pollution
articles.dek: KOLWEZI, Democratic Republic of Congo — In a small cinderblock home in the scrub beside a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine in Kolwezi, a mother shares a story of devastating loss.

paragraphs.en: KOLWEZI, Democratic Republic of Congo — In a small cinderblock home in the scrub beside a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine in Kolwezi, a mother shares a story of devastating loss.
paragraphs.zh: 刚果民主共和国科卢韦齐——在一座位于科卢韦齐一家中资铜钴矿旁边的灌木丛中的小砖房里，一位母亲讲述了一个关于惨痛损失的故事。

paragraphs.en: She believes pollution from the neighboring mine is responsible for her family's suffering.
paragraphs.zh: 她认为，邻近矿山的污染是导致她家人遭受苦难的原因。

paragraphs.en: She has lost three children. Two died at birth. A third suffered repeated nosebleeds before dying. One of her two surviving children has stunted growth.
paragraphs.zh: 她失去了三个孩子。两个孩子刚出生就夭折了。第三个孩子在去世前反复出现鼻出血。她幸存的两个孩子中有一个发育迟缓。

paragraphs.en: Now she and 26 other residents are taking the company to court in a rare attempt to hold alleged polluters accountable in the Democratic Republic of Congo. They are also suing the government, accusing it of failing to enforce environmental regulations.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，她和其他26名居民正在起诉该公司，这是在刚果民主共和国罕见的一次追究涉嫌污染者责任的尝试。他们还起诉了政府，指控政府未能执行环境法规。

paragraphs.en: Like other plaintiffs, she asked NPR not to identify her, fearing retribution from the company or government. Although the claimants' names are public in court documents, they want to avoid further exposure. Their lawyers also fear the plaintiffs could face intimidation from other locals.
paragraphs.zh: 与其他原告一样，她要求NPR不要透露她的身份，因为她担心会遭到公司或政府的报复。虽然法院文件中公开了原告的姓名，但他们希望避免进一步曝光。他们的律师也担心原告可能会受到其他当地人的恐吓。

paragraphs.en: "Our children are the first victims," she said, as the sun set over a nearby mound of mine tailings. "What we're hoping for is to see justice done."
paragraphs.zh: “我们的孩子是第一批受害者，”她说，这时太阳正落到附近的一座尾矿堆上。“我们希望看到正义得到伸张。”

paragraphs.en: The plaintiffs, whose case began Nov. 3, describe similar problems: contaminated water, nosebleeds, skin rashes, miscarriages and birth defects, which they blame on mining pollution.
paragraphs.zh: 原告的诉讼于11月3日开始，他们描述了类似的问题：水质污染、鼻出血、皮肤皮疹、流产和先天缺陷，他们将这些问题归咎于采矿污染。

paragraphs.en: The mine, known as COMMUS, is owned by Chinese multinational Zijin and lies in Kolwezi, a city of more than 500,000 people in the heart of Congo's copper belt, a southern region with vast mineral reserves.
paragraphs.zh: 该矿场名为COMMUS，由中国跨国公司紫金矿业所有，位于科卢韦齐，这是一座拥有50多万人口的城市，地处刚果铜矿带的中心，该地区位于刚果南部，拥有丰富的矿产储量。

articles.title: They attended Trump's meme coin dinner. It didn't go well
articles.dek: Headed to what some have called "the most exclusive dinner in the world," hosted by President Trump, crypto investor Morten Christensen and his young sister Gabriëlle Felen had butterflies in…

paragraphs.en: Headed to what some have called "the most exclusive dinner in the world," hosted by President Trump, crypto investor Morten Christensen and his young sister Gabriëlle Felen had butterflies in their stomachs.
paragraphs.zh: 在前往一些人称之为“世界上最尊贵的晚宴”的路上，由特朗普总统主办的这场晚宴让加密货币投资者Morten Christensen和他的妹妹Gabriëlle Felen感到紧张不已。

paragraphs.en: The dinner on Sunday, Nov. 22, was meant to reward the top holders of the president's meme coin — a type of crypto currency that Trump had launched just days before his inauguration.
paragraphs.zh: 11月22日（星期日）的晚宴旨在奖励总统迷因币的最大持有者，这种加密货币是特朗普在就职前几天推出的。

paragraphs.en: "I'm excited!," said Christensen. "It's always nice to dress up for an event. My sister looks amazing!"
paragraphs.zh: “我很兴奋！”克里斯滕森说。“为参加活动盛装打扮总是很棒。我妹妹看起来太棒了！”

paragraphs.en: Christensen — the founder of a crypto website called Airdrop Alert — is a veteran trader who got the crypto bug as far back as 2013. He has attended each of the previous two events Trump has held for the top holders of his meme coin.
paragraphs.zh: 克里斯滕森是名为Airdrop Alert的加密货币网站的创始人，他是一位资深交易员，早在2013年就迷上了加密货币。他参加了特朗普此前为他的迷因币顶级持有者举办的两场活动。

paragraphs.en: For him it was just a chance to get a glimpse of the president. Christensen said that he's not political — and always advises others to "never buy a political meme coin ever."
paragraphs.zh: 对他来说，这只是一个一睹总统风采的机会。克里斯滕森表示，他并不关心政治，并且总是建议其他人“永远不要购买政治迷因币”。

paragraphs.en: The events have been intensely controversial. Anti-corruption activists have said they pose enormous conflicts of interest concerns, effectively rewarding those who buy the most coins with access to the president. Top buyers get the closest access.
paragraphs.zh: 这些活动备受争议。反腐败活动人士表示，这些活动引发了巨大的利益冲突问题，实际上是对购买最多代币的人给予接触总统的奖励。购买量最大的买家可以获得最亲密的接触机会。

paragraphs.en: Christensen was unsure if he would attend this latest dinner. But a sharp drop in the value of Trump's meme coin — from a peak of over $70 in January 2025 to now less than a dollar — had sharply reduced the cost of qualifying as a top holder, which provides access to the dinner.
paragraphs.zh: 克里斯滕森不确定自己是否会参加这次最新的晚宴。但特朗普的迷因币价值大幅下跌——从2025年1月的峰值70多美元跌至现在的不到1美元——这大大降低了成为顶级持有者的成本，而顶级持有者有资格参加晚宴。

paragraphs.en: And, above all, it was a chance to bring his sister Felen for the ride.
paragraphs.zh: 最重要的是，他有机会带上妹妹Felen一起骑行。

paragraphs.en: On Sunday night, Christensen and Felen agreed to provide NPR with voice memos through an event that turned out to be something they likely won't forget.
paragraphs.zh: 周日晚上，克里斯滕森和费伦同意通过一场他们可能永远不会忘记的活动，向NPR提供语音备忘录。

articles.title: Trump claims credit as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
articles.dek: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO of the world's largest chipmaker on Monday, sending the company's stock soaring as President Trump claimed credit for brokering his close ally's return.

paragraphs.en: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO of the world's largest chipmaker on Monday, sending the company's stock soaring as President Trump claimed credit for brokering his close ally's return.
paragraphs.zh: 周一，英伟达（Nvidia）重新任命黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）为这家全球最大芯片制造商的首席执行官，该公司股价应声飙升，而特朗普总统则宣称自己促成了这位亲密盟友的回归。

paragraphs.en: It was a stunning reversal of fortune for Huang. He resigned less than two weeks ago, following news reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of being a Chinese spy.
paragraphs.zh: 这对黄来说是命运的惊人逆转。在有关他婚外情的报道传出后，他于不到两周前辞职。这些报道称，他的婚外情对象中包括一名被美国情报机构怀疑是中国间谍的女性。

paragraphs.en: In a statement put out just before the market opened, Nvidia said its board voted unanimously in favor of bringing back Huang after a series of conversations and meetings, as well as input from people at "senior levels" of the U.S. government. "Based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk," the board said.
paragraphs.zh: 英伟达在市场开盘前发布的一份声明中表示，经过一系列的讨论和会议，以及美国政府“高层”人士的意见，其董事会一致投票赞成让黄仁勋复职。董事会表示：“根据这些意见，董事会有信心认为黄先生的复职不会对国家安全构成风险。”

paragraphs.en: Nvidia's stock price shot up more than 30% on Monday, helping buoy stock indexes after last week's losses, which were driven by the tech sector.
paragraphs.zh: 英伟达的股价周一飙升逾30%，帮助提振了在上周受科技板块拖累而下跌的股市指数。

paragraphs.en: Trump endorsed the move, calling it the "correct and proper decision" in a social media post. He said Huang's leadership was needed "in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy."
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普在社交媒体帖文中表示支持这一举措，称其为“正确且恰当的决定”。他说，需要黄仁勋的领导力，“以确保不仅是公司的成功和繁荣，还有美国经济的成功和繁荣。”

paragraphs.en: The president had repeatedly urged Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang as CEO in public comments and on social media. In a lengthy interview with CNBC Monday morning, Trump claimed his influence helped Huang get his job back.
paragraphs.zh: 特朗普总统曾在公开场合和社交媒体上多次敦促英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官职务。在周一上午接受CNBC的长时间采访中，特朗普声称他的影响力帮助黄仁勋重获职位。

paragraphs.en: "I don't want to say, but basically I was represented at the board," the president said, in response to a question about a report in Semafor that he had called directly into the Nvidia board meeting.
paragraphs.zh: 在回答有关Semafor的一篇报道的问题时，该总裁表示：“我不想多说，但基本上我在董事会是有代表的。”该报道称，他曾直接致电参加Nvidia的董事会会议。

paragraphs.en: "I spoke to them. Let me just put it that way. And I convinced them," Trump told CNBC. "And I must tell you, it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago."
paragraphs.zh: “我和他们谈过了。我就这么说吧。我让他们相信了，”特朗普对CNBC表示。“我必须告诉你们，昨天说服他们比一个半星期前容易得多。”

paragraphs.en: He later added: "When the stock starts dropping forty, fifty percent, it was a lot easier for me to do it yesterday than it would have been."
paragraphs.zh: 他后来补充道：“当股价开始下跌40%、50%时，我昨天采取行动要比现在容易得多。”

articles.title: Meet Colombia's fuzzy 'water guardians'
articles.dek: MONGUÍ, Colombia — Moisés Moreno greets visitors at his greenhouse 10,000 feet high in the Andes Mountains. Underneath the plastic roof, he nurtures tiny seedlings that can grow to be 30-feet tall.

paragraphs.en: MONGUÍ, Colombia — Moisés Moreno greets visitors at his greenhouse 10,000 feet high in the Andes Mountains. Underneath the plastic roof, he nurtures tiny seedlings that can grow to be 30-feet tall.
paragraphs.zh: 哥伦比亚蒙圭——Moisés Moreno 在位于安第斯山脉海拔 10000 英尺的温室里迎接游客。在塑料棚顶下，他悉心培育着细小的幼苗，这些幼苗长大后可长到30英尺高。

paragraphs.en: "Do you know anything about frailejons?" Moreno asks his visitors, who are mostly clueless.
paragraphs.zh: “你们对弗莱洪有什么了解吗？” 莫雷诺问他的访客，他们大多一无所知。

paragraphs.en: Related to the sunflower, frailejons are the iconic flora of Colombia's high mountain wetlands, which are known as páramos, and are vital for the country's water supply.
paragraphs.zh: 弗莱莱洪与向日葵同属一科，是哥伦比亚高山湿地（被称为“páramos”）的标志性植物，对该国的供水至关重要。

paragraphs.en: The wooly fuzz on their leaves protect frailejons from the cold and absorb water from the cloud cover. This helps maintain moisture in the páramos, which are the source of major rivers, and much of Colombia's water.
paragraphs.zh: 叶子上的绒毛可以保护弗雷洪植物免受寒冷，并从云层中吸收水分。这有助于保持高寒草甸的水分，而高寒草甸是主要河流以及哥伦比亚大部分水源的源头。

paragraphs.en: But frailejons and the páramos where they grow face a growing array of threats, including farmers, cattle ranchers and coal miners who are gradually pushing higher into the Andes. In addition, climate change is warming the mountains, allowing invasive species to survive at higher altitudes and disrupt their fragile ecosystems.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，弗雷莱洪植物及其生长的帕拉莫正面临着越来越多的威胁，包括正逐步向安第斯山脉更高处推进的农民、牧场主和煤矿工人。此外，气候变化正在使山区变暖，使入侵物种能够在更高海拔地区生存，并破坏脆弱的生态系统。

paragraphs.en: Of the nearly 150 species of frailejons, two-thirds are at risk and 17 are endangered, says Mauricio Diazgranados, a Colombian expert on the plant who is chief science officer at the New York Botanical Garden.
paragraphs.zh: 哥伦比亚植物专家、纽约植物园首席科学官毛里西奥·迪亚兹格拉纳多斯（Mauricio Diazgranados）表示，在近150种弗莱莱洪植物中，有三分之二面临威胁，其中17种濒临灭绝。

paragraphs.en: "They are a keystone species for maintaining the páramos and play a key role in water production," he says. "But most frailejons are in trouble,"
paragraphs.zh: “它们是维持高寒草甸的伞物种，在水源涵养方面发挥着关键作用。”他说，“但大多数弗莱洪植物都面临困境。”

paragraphs.en: When explorers first spotted the shrubs mysteriously protruding from the mountain fog centuries ago, they reminded them of hooded monks. Hence the name frailejon, which is Spanish for "big friar."
paragraphs.zh: 几个世纪前，当探险家们第一次看到这些灌木丛神秘地从山间雾气中冒出来时，它们让探险家们想起了头戴兜帽的僧侣。因此，它们得名“frailejon”，在西班牙语中意为“大修士”。

paragraphs.en: The long, thin leaves of some species bend toward the sky and resemble palm fronds. Many are stout in the middle because, rather than falling to the ground, their dying leaves slump down to form a brownish outer shell to their trunks.
paragraphs.zh: 有些物种的叶子又长又细，向天空弯曲，形似棕榈叶。许多龙血树的中间部分很粗壮，因为它们的枯叶不会掉落到地上，而是下垂形成棕褐色的外壳包裹在树干上。

articles.title: Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
articles.dek: During the Jim Crow Era, Black families traveling Route 66, the historic highway that ran more than 2,000 miles from Chicago to Los Angeles, needed to carry food and gas with them. Most…

paragraphs.en: During the Jim Crow Era, Black families traveling Route 66, the historic highway that ran more than 2,000 miles from Chicago to Los Angeles, needed to carry food and gas with them. Most restaurants, gas stations and motels wouldn't serve them.
paragraphs.zh: 在吉姆·克劳时代，黑人家庭在66号公路上旅行时需要随身携带食物和汽油。这条历史悠久的公路从芝加哥一直延伸到洛杉矶，全长超过2000英里。大多数餐厅、加油站和汽车旅馆都不愿意为他们提供服务。

paragraphs.en: But there was one place they were guaranteed to find respite: a small, family-owned business just east of Oklahoma City that offered fuel, food and a place to stop for the night. The Threatt Filling Station, according to the National Trust for Historic Preservation, was the only known Black-owned and operated gas station along the famous Mother Road.
paragraphs.zh: 但有一个地方可以让他们安心歇脚：位于俄克拉荷马城以东的一家小型家族企业，这里提供燃油、食物和过夜场所。据美国国家历史保护信托基金会称，Threatt加油站是著名的“母亲之路”沿线唯一一家已知由黑人拥有和经营的加油站。

paragraphs.en: "Grandpa took care of whatever they needed to have," said Linda Fisher, the granddaughter of the station's founder, Allen Threatt Sr. Her family still owns the station and the 150 acres around it.
paragraphs.zh: “爷爷会满足他们的所有需求。”车站创始人大卫·特雷特（Allen Threatt Sr.）的孙女琳达·费舍尔（Linda Fisher）说道。她的家人至今仍拥有该车站及其周围150英亩的土地。

paragraphs.en: "If they didn't have any food, they fed them," she said. "If they needed some kind of shelter or blankets or those types of things, Grandpa and Grandma made sure they got those kinds of things."
paragraphs.zh: “如果他们没有食物，爷爷奶奶就会给他们吃的，”她说。“如果他们需要某种住所、毯子或类似的东西，爷爷奶奶就会想办法让他们得到这些东西。”

paragraphs.en: Threatt moved from Alabama to the farming community of Luther, Okla., in the early 1900s as part of the Great Migration. His father had been born into slavery, and Threatt and his wife, Alberta, seeking stability and refuge, wanted their own farm.
paragraphs.zh: 20 世纪初，Threatt 随大迁徙的浪潮从阿拉巴马州迁至俄克拉荷马州卢瑟的农业社区。他的父亲生来就是奴隶，Threatt和妻子Alberta为了寻求稳定和庇护，希望拥有自己的农场。

paragraphs.en: At the time, Oklahoma was a place where Black migrants could own land and form their own towns. Between 1865 and 1920, Black Americans settled more than 50 "all-Black" municipalities in Oklahoma, the largest number of any state.
paragraphs.zh: 当时，俄克拉荷马州是黑人移民可以拥有土地并建立自己城镇的地方。1865 年至 1920 年间，黑人美国人在俄克拉荷马州建立了 50 多个“全黑人”城镇，数量之多在全美各州中名列前茅。

paragraphs.en: But Oklahoma also had its issues — by the time of the Great Depression, many of those all-Black towns had ceased to exist. And there was a rise in "sundown towns": all-white communities that warned non-white people to get out before dark, or they would face violence or police harassment. There was a sundown town on either side of the filling station during the Jim Crow era, Fisher said.
paragraphs.zh: 但俄克拉荷马州也有自己的问题——到大萧条时期，许多全黑人城镇已不复存在。“日落镇”的数量也有所增加：“日落镇”是全白人社区，他们警告非白人要在天黑前离开，否则将面临暴力或警察骚扰。Fisher说，在吉姆·克劳时代，加油站的两侧都有一个日落镇。

paragraphs.en: But at the Threatt Filling Station, "everyone was welcome," Fisher said.
paragraphs.zh: 但菲舍尔说，在特雷特加油站，“人人皆受欢迎”。

articles.title: Ukraine war spilling into NATO territory
articles.dek: The war between Russia and Ukraine once again creeps onto European territory – from attacks on ships to missiles in Poland and fresh allegations of Russian operations inside Denmark.

paragraphs.en: The war between Russia and Ukraine once again creeps onto European territory – from attacks on ships to missiles in Poland and fresh allegations of Russian operations inside Denmark.
paragraphs.zh: 俄罗斯与乌克兰之间的战争再次蔓延到欧洲领土——从对船只的袭击到波兰的导弹袭击，以及针对俄罗斯在丹麦内部行动的新指控。

paragraphs.en: A Russian ship was set ablaze after it was struck by a drone in the Baltic Sea. Yet another sign that the war in Ukraine is, at times, spilling over into the rest of Europe. This comes just days after President Trump called Russian President Vladimir Putin his friend. Teri Schultz joins us now from Brussels. Teri, let's start in the Gulf of Finland. A Russian cargo ship was hit by a drone there Saturday and caught fire. What's the latest on that?
paragraphs.zh: 一艘俄罗斯船在波罗的海被无人机击中后起火。这又是一个迹象，显示乌克兰战争有时会蔓延到欧洲其他地区。这发生在特朗普总统称俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京为他的朋友几天之后。特里·舒尔茨现在从布鲁塞尔加入我们。特里，让我们从芬兰湾开始。上周六，一艘俄罗斯货船在那里被无人机击中并起火。最新情况如何？

paragraphs.en: TERI SCHULTZ, BYLINE: Well, a few hours ago, Rob, Russia took control of this cargo ship, the Sparta II, and towed it out of Finnish waters a day after, as you mentioned, it was hit by a drone. The crew was rescued by another Russian vessel traveling nearby at the time of the strike. Now, the attack is presumed to have come from Ukraine, but Kyiv has not yet claimed responsibility. Finnish President Alexander Stubb referred to the incident as an unfortunate reminder that the, quote, "consequences of Russia's war of aggression are also visible in our region." Interestingly, teams from both Finland and neighboring Estonia came Saturday and helped Russian ships try to put out the fire on board. Stubb thanked all of those involved for what he called responsible and professional actions.
paragraphs.zh: 特里·舒尔茨(Teri Schultz) 署名：几小时前，罗布，俄罗斯控制了这艘货船“斯巴达二号”(Sparta II)，并将其从芬兰水域拖出，正如你提到的，这发生在它被无人机击中后的第二天。当时另一艘在附近航行的俄罗斯船只救出了船员。目前，攻击被认为是来自乌克兰，但基辅尚未承认责任。芬兰总统亚历山大·斯图布(Alexander Stubb) 将此次事件称为一个不幸的提醒，引用原话：“俄罗斯侵略战争的后果在我们地区也是显而易见的。”有趣的是，来自芬兰和邻国爱沙尼亚的团队在周六到达，并帮助俄罗斯船只试图扑灭船上的火灾。斯图布感谢所有参与人员，他称其为负责任且专业的行动。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: So if the Sparta II was in the service of the Russian military, why didn't Finland seize the ship to put it out of business?
paragraphs.zh: 施密茨：所以如果斯巴达II号为俄罗斯军方服务，为什么芬兰没有扣押这艘船以使其停运呢？

paragraphs.en: SCHULTZ: There was a lot of talk about this in Finland because this ship transports weapons and other supplies to Russia to use against Ukraine. And the vessel itself is under U.S. and U.K. sanctions, and its owner is under European Union sanctions. But the conclusion this time was that it would create too big an environmental hazard to keep it in Finnish waters. Here's how it was described in a press conference by Jukka-Pekka Lumilahti, the director of sea operations for the Finnish Border Guard.
paragraphs.zh: 舒尔茨：在芬兰，这件事引起了很多讨论，因为这艘船向俄罗斯运送武器和其他物资，用于对抗乌克兰。而且这艘船本身受到美国和英国的制裁，其船东也受到欧盟的制裁。但这次的结论是，将其留在芬兰水域会造成过大的环境风险。在一次新闻发布会上，芬兰边境警卫队海上行动主管尤卡-佩卡·卢米拉希是这样描述的。

paragraphs.en: JUKKA-PEKKA LUMILAHTI: (Through interpreter) If we would let the vessel burn, it would most likely sink. And after that, it would cause a major environmental risk for Finland and Estonia.
paragraphs.zh: JUKKA-PEKKA LUMILAHTI：（通过翻译）如果我们让船只燃烧，它很可能会沉没。之后，这将对芬兰和爱沙尼亚造成重大环境风险。

paragraphs.en: SCHULTZ: So as much as Finland would be pleased to take a military cargo ship out of Moscow's arsenal, in this case, they were basically saying good riddance.
paragraphs.zh: 舒尔茨：所以，尽管芬兰很高兴能从莫斯科的军火库里拿走一艘军用货船，但在这种情况下，他们基本上是在说再见了，好走不送。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: So Ukraine is not the only one launching far-reaching strikes. Last Friday, Russia launched missiles into Polish territory. And I understand that you were there covering a nearby military exercise involving nearly a dozen countries, and it was that that was suspected to be Russia's reason for doing this, right?
paragraphs.zh: SCHMITZ：所以乌克兰并不是唯一发动远程打击的国家。上周五，俄罗斯向波兰领土发射了导弹。据我了解，你当时正在那里报道一次涉及近十多个国家的附近军事演习，而这次演习被怀疑是俄罗斯这样做的原因，对吧？

paragraphs.en: SCHULTZ: Yeah, that's right. There were three Russian cruise missiles that landed between 30 and 60 miles from this military exercise, which was training forces for what's envisioned to eventually be a peace-monitoring mission in post-war Ukraine. At the time, all we knew on the ground was that there were multiple air alerts, at one time even telling us to take cover. And that happens often in Poland, especially at that location just over a hundred miles from the Ukrainian border. But this is particularly risky for the Russians, as they never know whether they'll kill people from a NATO country on the ground. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte was asked by a crowd of reporters in Warsaw whether the alliance can do anything to stop these Russian incursions.
paragraphs.zh: 舒尔茨：是的，没错。有三枚俄罗斯巡航导弹落在距离这次军演大约30到60英里的地方，这次军演是为了训练部队参与预计将来在战后乌克兰执行的和平观察任务。当时，我们在现场所知道的只是出现了多次空袭警报，有一次甚至告诉我们要寻找掩护。在波兰，这种情况经常发生，特别是在距离乌克兰边境刚刚一百多英里的那个地点。但这对俄罗斯人来说尤其危险，因为他们永远不知道是否会杀到北约国家的人员。北约秘书长马克·吕特在华沙被一群记者问到，联盟是否能采取任何措施阻止这些俄罗斯的入侵。

articles.title: He expected a small-business loan. He got a 7-year nightmare
articles.dek: GLENDALE, Calif. — Sitting at his desk, tucked into a corner of his teenage bedroom — a place where he'd never intended to return, well into middle age — Vahe Shahinian rereads the emails that…

paragraphs.en: GLENDALE, Calif. — Sitting at his desk, tucked into a corner of his teenage bedroom — a place where he'd never intended to return, well into middle age — Vahe Shahinian rereads the emails that split his life into before and after.
paragraphs.zh: 加利福尼亚州格伦代尔——坐在他的书桌前，书桌被安置在他青少年时期的卧室一角——这是一个他从未打算在中年以后回来的地方——瓦赫·沙希尼安重读那些将他的人生划分为之前和之后的电子邮件。

paragraphs.en: A broker was offering to fund Shahinian's small business with a line of credit worth $750,000.
paragraphs.zh: 一位经纪人正在提供资金支持Shahinian的小企业，额度为75万美元的信用额度。

paragraphs.en: It was 2019, and Shahinian's company soared, like a miniature Live Nation-Ticketmaster, selling tickets and producing concerts around Los Angeles and beyond. He imagined how much he could do with stable funding.
paragraphs.zh: 那是2019年，沙希尼安的公司蒸蒸日上，就像一个迷你版的Live Nation-Ticketmaster，在洛杉矶及其他地区售票并制作演唱会。他设想如果有稳定的资金支持，他能做多少事情。

paragraphs.en: The pitch had a catch: Shahinian would first accept a third of the sum and start paying it back immediately, in daily installments of $3,600. After 30 days, he could access the rest of the money. He crunched the numbers, followed up with questions — and took the deal.
paragraphs.zh: 这个提议有一个附加条件：Shahinian 首先会接受总额的三分之一，并立即开始偿还，每天分期支付 3,600 美元。30 天后，他才能使用剩余的钱。他算了算账，提出了一些问题——然后接受了这个协议。

paragraphs.en: Shahinian sent the daily payments, he says, for 30 days. Then 40. Then 50.
paragraphs.zh: Shahinian说，他每天支付了30天。然后是40天。然后是50天。

paragraphs.en: "From that day," he says, "it's been one long day, one long nightmare."
paragraphs.zh: “从那一天起，”他说，“就像是一整天，一场漫长的噩梦。”

paragraphs.en: For seven years, Shahinian has been mired in the shadowy industry that is now the fastest-growing source of funding for small business in the United States. It's largely unregulated, promising fast money at a tremendous cost. And Shahinian's lawsuit against his funders could become one of the first of its kind to go to trial.
paragraphs.zh: 七年来，Shahinian一直陷在这个如今成为美国小企业最快增长资金来源的阴暗行业中。它在很大程度上不受监管，承诺快速赚钱，但代价巨大。而Shahinian针对他的资金方提起的诉讼可能成为首批将开庭审理的此类案件之一。

paragraphs.en: Before the "incident," as Shahinian calls his fateful deal, he'd been in business for 15 years, building his company from a side hustle into his main source of income.
paragraphs.zh: 在沙希尼安所称的那次“事件”发生之前，他已经经营了十五年的生意，将公司从副业发展成主要收入来源。

articles.title: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules
articles.dek: GENEVA — Diplomats meeting at the United Nations in Geneva have agreed to start discussing options to regulate lethal autonomous weapons, often called "killer robots."

paragraphs.en: GENEVA — Diplomats meeting at the United Nations in Geneva have agreed to start discussing options to regulate lethal autonomous weapons, often called "killer robots."
paragraphs.zh: 日内瓦——在日内瓦联合国会晤的外交官们已经同意开始讨论规范致命自主武器的选项，这种武器通常被称为“杀手机器人”。

paragraphs.en: After a week of negotiations that dragged on until the small hours of Saturday morning, a compromise emerged: countries would have two years to suggest regulations that could be legally binding, but could also be optional.
paragraphs.zh: 经过一周的谈判，谈判一直拖到周六凌晨，达成了一个妥协：各国将有两年的时间提出可能具有法律约束力但也可以是可选的规定。

paragraphs.en: Bleary-eyed negotiators insisted the agreement was better than nothing and showed the U.N.'s disarmament process could still function. But for many humanitarian organizations and many countries, the deal falls far short of what they had hoped for.
paragraphs.zh: 眼睛昏花的谈判代表坚持认为，这项协议总比没有好，并显示联合国的裁军进程仍然可以运作。但对于许多人道主义组织和许多国家来说，这项协议远未达到他们的期望。

paragraphs.en: Before the negotiations got underway, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the guardian of the Geneva Conventions, said it was urgent for legally binding rules to be drafted within a year. That call was backed by the U.N. secretary-general and by Pope Leo.
paragraphs.zh: 在谈判开始之前，作为日内瓦公约的守护者的红十字国际委员会表示，迫切需要在一年内起草具有法律约束力的规则。这一呼吁得到了联合国秘书长和教皇利奥的支持。

paragraphs.en: Their concerns stem from the kind of warfare we are now seeing. In Ukraine, Sudan and Gaza, civilians are being killed by semi-autonomous drones. This year in Sudan, 80% of civilian deaths were caused by drones according to the U.N.
paragraphs.zh: 他们的担忧源于我们现在所看到的战争类型。在乌克兰、苏丹和加沙，平民正遭到半自主无人机的杀害。据联合国称，今年在苏丹，80%的平民死亡是由无人机造成的。

paragraphs.en: Humans remain, albeit very remotely, in control for now, but humanitarian organizations fear we are on the verge of seeing artificial intelligence-assisted weapons make the decision to kill entirely on their own.
paragraphs.zh: 人类仍然暂时处于控制之中，尽管控制力非常有限，但人道主义组织担心，我们正处于人工智能辅助武器完全自主作出杀戮决定的边缘。

paragraphs.en: "There is a fundamental ethical concern with having what are essentially these life-and-death decisions determined by programming, determined by an algorithm," said ICRC legal adviser Georgia Hinds. "That's not something that you can fix with better technology. That is a moral red line that we cannot cross."
paragraphs.zh: 红十字国际委员会法律顾问乔治亚·欣兹表示：“让本质上关乎生死的决定由程序、由算法来决定，这是一个根本的伦理问题。这不是通过更好的技术就能解决的。这是一条我们不能跨越的道德红线。”

paragraphs.en: No one went into the negotiations thinking they would be easy; some of the world's most powerful countries, among them the U.S., Russia and Israel, had already indicated their reluctance to agree to binding regulations.
paragraphs.zh: 没有人进入谈判时认为事情会很容易；世界上一些最强大的国家，其中包括美国、俄罗斯和以色列，已经表示不愿意同意有约束力的规定。

articles.title: What it's like at a climate conference as talks collapse
articles.dek: What it's like in the halls of a climate conference as it collapses

paragraphs.en: What it's like in the halls of a climate conference as it collapses
paragraphs.zh: 气候会议崩溃时大堂里的情形

paragraphs.en: After two weeks of negotiations, international climate talks fail to reach an agreement. NPR's Rachel Waldholz was in Turkey for the conference.
paragraphs.zh: 经过两周的谈判，国际气候会议未能达成协议。NPR的Rachel Waldholz参加了在土耳其举行的会议。

paragraphs.en: International climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, ended today after negotiations fell apart. NPR's Rachel Waldholz has been at the conference and sent us this report.
paragraphs.zh: 土耳其安塔利亚的国际气候谈判在谈判破裂后于今天结束。美国国家公共电台的拉切尔·沃尔德霍尔茨一直在现场参加会议，并向我们发送了这份报道。

paragraphs.en: RACHEL WALDHOLZ, BYLINE: I'm here in the Antalya Expo Center, which, for the past two weeks, has been packed with some 70,000 people who came to the COP31 climate conference. Now it's almost completely empty. In fact, they're disassembling parts of the venue around me. The climate talks ran two days past their scheduled end. By the time the gavel fell, many negotiators had already left to catch their flights home. Australia climate chief Chris Bowen led the negotiations.
paragraphs.zh: 瑞切尔·沃尔德霍尔茨（RACHEL WALDHOLZ），署名：我现在在安塔利亚博览中心，在过去的两周里，这里挤满了大约7万名参加联合国气候变化大会（COP31）的人。现在这里几乎已经空无一人。实际上，他们正在我周围拆卸场馆的一部分设施。气候谈判比预定时间延长了两天。等到会议主席敲下木槌时，许多谈判代表已经离开赶回家。澳大利亚气候首席代表克里斯·鲍文（Chris Bowen）主持了此次谈判。

paragraphs.en: CHRIS BOWEN: I haven't slept for the last three nights, been negotiating all the way through, but more importantly, people on delegations came at it and gave it everything they had.
paragraphs.zh: 克里斯·鲍文：我在过去三晚都没睡觉，一直在进行谈判，但更重要的是，代表团的人们全力以赴地投入其中。

paragraphs.en: WALDHOLZ: Delegates came to Antalya with long wish lists, from electrifying more of the global economy to money for developing countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change. Looming over it all is that this is the first summit to squarely face the reality that the planet will miss a key target of the Paris Climate Agreement, reaching warming of 1.5 degrees Celsius or 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit above pre-Industrial levels. The U.N. says limiting that overshoot requires cutting the use of fossil fuels nearly in half in the next 10 to 15 years. Many countries wanted an agreement explicitly calling for a transition away from coal, oil and natural gas. But big oil-producing countries, like Saudi Arabia, blocked any mention of fossil fuels. Ultimately, the European Union decided no deal was better than the deal on the table. Darragh O'Brien is Ireland's environment minister.
paragraphs.zh: 瓦尔德霍尔茨：代表们带着长长的愿望清单来到安塔利亚，从加速全球经济电气化到为发展中国家提供资金以应对气候变化的影响。笼罩在这一切之上的是，这是首次首脑会议正面面对一个现实：地球将无法实现《巴黎气候协定》的关键目标，即全球气温较工业化前水平升高控制在1.5摄氏度或2.7华氏度以内。联合国表示，要限制超标，需要在未来10到15年内将化石燃料的使用量几乎减半。许多国家希望达成一项明确要求逐步摆脱煤炭、石油和天然气的协议。但像沙特阿拉伯这样的主要产油国阻止了关于化石燃料的任何提及。最终，欧盟决定，没有协议比现有协议更好。达拉·奥布赖恩是爱尔兰环境部长。

paragraphs.en: DARRAGH O'BRIEN: We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change.
paragraphs.zh: DARRAGH O'BRIEN：我们不会支持一项封面决定或安塔利亚协议，如果它甚至没有提到化石燃料，而化石燃料是气候变化的关键驱动因素。

paragraphs.en: WALDHOLZ: Many negotiators left the expo center dragging their suitcases on the way to the airport. They'll pick up negotiations next year at the next climate summit in Ethiopia. I'm Rachel Waldholz in Antalya, Turkey.
paragraphs.zh: 瓦尔德霍尔茨：许多谈判代表离开博览中心时拖着行李箱前往机场。他们将在明年埃塞俄比亚举行的下一次气候峰会上继续谈判。我是雷切尔·瓦尔德霍尔茨，来自土耳其安塔利亚。
