articles.title: Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
articles.dek: JOHANNESBURG — It's an ordinary Saturday morning in Alexandra township, known simply as Alex or sometimes dubbed Gomora, a reference to the biblical city of Gomorrah that was known for its wickedness.

paragraphs.en: JOHANNESBURG — It's an ordinary Saturday morning in Alexandra township, known simply as Alex or sometimes dubbed Gomora, a reference to the biblical city of Gomorrah that was known for its wickedness.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰内斯堡——这是亚历山德拉镇的一个普通星期六早晨，这里通常被简称为亚历克斯，有时也被称为戈莫拉，取名自圣经中的罪恶城市戈摩拉。

paragraphs.en: That nickname stems from Alexandra's high crime rates. It's a high-density area, where modest brick houses and tin shacks stretch as far as the eye can see and rotting garbage piles up along potholed streets.
paragraphs.zh: 这个绰号源自亚历山德拉的高犯罪率。这里是一个高密度地区，简陋的砖房和铁皮棚一直延伸到视线尽头，坑洼的街道上堆积着腐烂的垃圾。

paragraphs.en: But that image doesn't intrude on an event at a small building at the Kwabhekilanga Sports Ground. There's a palpable sense of excitement. Something different is happening this weekend and community members have turned up for it.
paragraphs.zh: 但那幅画面并没有干扰Kwabhekilanga体育场小建筑中的活动。现场充满了明显的兴奋感。这个周末发生了一些不同寻常的事情，社区成员都赶来了。

paragraphs.en: It's a book launch for a collection entitled From Gomora to the World. Stories from Alex. The seven stories in the self-published anthology have been written by children from the township who attend a free weekly literacy program.
paragraphs.zh: 这是《从戈莫拉到世界——亚历克斯的故事》一书的发布会。这本自费出版的选集中的七个故事由来自该镇的孩子们创作，他们参加一个免费的每周读写项目。

paragraphs.en: South Africa is in the midst of a literacy crisis, with one international study showing a majority of 10-year-olds — some 81% — are unable to read for meaning in any of South Africa's 12 official languages.
paragraphs.zh: 南非正处于识字危机之中，一项国际研究显示，大多数10岁的儿童——约81%——无法用南非的12种官方语言中的任何一种进行意义阅读。

paragraphs.en: The grassroots program Read Alex has been trying to change this, offering a weekend reading club, mainly in English, to instill a love of books in children. Launched by the Run Alex Athletics Club, it has about 50 participants. Among the activities: an annual public speaking competition, two spelling bees and a book drive on Mandela Day every year that brings in about 500 volumes — some of which the kids take home and some of which go to libraries.
paragraphs.zh: 基层项目“Read Alex”一直在试图改变这种状况，提供一个主要用英语进行的周末阅读俱乐部，以培养儿童对书籍的热爱。该项目由“Run Alex Athletics Club”发起，约有50名参与者。活动包括：每年的公开演讲比赛、两场拼写比赛，以及每年曼德拉日举行的图书募捐活动，筹集约500本书——其中一些让孩子们带回家，另一些则捐给图书馆。

paragraphs.en: Now, not only are the children getting to practice their reading, some of them have tried their hand at writing their own stories.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，孩子们不仅可以练习阅读，其中一些孩子还尝试写自己的故事。

paragraphs.en: The newly published authors sit up front, ready to sign the pile of freshly-printed books for sale and answer questions about their process.

articles.title: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?
articles.dek: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Robert Daly, director of the program on US China relations at University of Maryland's School of Public Policy, about President Trump's trip to China this week.

paragraphs.en: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Robert Daly, director of the program on US China relations at University of Maryland's School of Public Policy, about President Trump's trip to China this week.
paragraphs.zh: 美国国家公共电台（NPR）的罗伯·施密茨（Rob Schmitz）与马里兰大学公共政策学院中美关系项目主任罗伯特·戴利（Robert Daly）就特朗普总统本周对中国的访问进行了访谈。

paragraphs.en: When the president goes on a big diplomatic trip, it's not always clear what's happening in all those meetings they go to. That was true during President Trump's trip to China this week, but there were intriguing public moments.
paragraphs.zh: 当总统进行重大外交访问时，他所参加的所有会议的具体情况并不总是很清楚。本周特朗普总统访华期间也是如此，但也有一些引人注目的公开场合。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: A group of children chanted, warm welcome, over and over, as Xi Jinping met Trump on the tarmac. Now add a third leader to the mix.
paragraphs.zh: SCHMITZ：习近平在停机坪上与特朗普会面时，一群孩子一遍又一遍地高呼“热烈欢迎”。现在，再加入第三位领导人。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: That was Vladimir Putin, who's also a friend of Xi Jinping's, though the two may preside over an uneasy alliance. The stakes were high. Trump is looking for a breakthrough on nuclear weapons control. The U.S. and China are in a faceoff over AI, and a deal to end the bloodshed in Ukraine has been elusive.
paragraphs.zh: SCHMITZ：那是弗拉基米尔·普京，他也是习近平的朋友，尽管两人可能领导着一个并不稳固的联盟。利害关系重大。特朗普正在寻求在核武器控制方面取得突破。美国和中国正在人工智能问题上针锋相对，而结束乌克兰流血冲突的协议一直遥不可及。

paragraphs.en: Now that the summit's over, we're joined by someone who can help make sense of what happened. Robert Daly was a U.S. foreign service officer in China and now directs the program on U.S.-China relations at the University of Maryland School of Public Policy. And he's here with me in the studio. Welcome.
paragraphs.zh: 峰会已经结束，现在我们请来了一位嘉宾，他将帮助我们理解峰会期间发生的事情。罗伯特·戴利曾是美国驻华外交官，现任马里兰大学公共政策学院中美关系项目主任。他现在和我一起在演播室。欢迎。

paragraphs.en: DALY: Xi Jinping - as always, his first goal is performative. It is to have the Chinese people see him as a world leader, beneficent, competent, hosting others who are coming somewhat cap in hand, at least in a very friendly way, to China. There's a very ancient saying in Chinese, (speaking Chinese), which means the 10,000 kingdoms all come to the center here. And Xi has been hosting an awful lot of leaders recently.
paragraphs.zh: 戴利：习近平——一如既往，他的首要目标是表演性。那就是让中国人民将他视为一位仁慈、干练的世界领袖，接待那些多少有些低声下气地、至少是以非常友好的方式前来中国的其他国家领导人。中国有一句非常古老的俗语，（用中文说），意思是万国来朝。习近平最近接待了非常多的领导人。

paragraphs.en: DALY: He did very well from the Chinese point of view. I think that the hug of Donald Trump - we tend to see that from an American point of view as being friendly. Now, whether that's performative, friendship or truly felt is only for them to say. But for the Chinese, that's an unusually warm and humanizing move for Xi. Even the Chinese people will complain that their leaders are often too stayed, too in control. And this warmth, I think, also makes him look good, as does all the formal ceremony.
paragraphs.zh: 戴利：从中国的角度来看，他做得非常好。我认为，唐纳德·特朗普的拥抱——我们倾向于从美国的角度来看待这一举动，认为这是友好的表现。至于那是表演性的友谊还是真情实感，只有他们自己知道。但对于中国人来说，这是习近平一个非常热情、富有亲和力的举动。就连中国人民也会抱怨说，他们的领导人往往过于拘谨，过于克制。我认为，这种热情也让他看起来很棒，所有正式的仪式也是如此。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: We also had Vladimir Putin there, the president of Russia. What was his goal at this meeting?
paragraphs.zh: SCHMITZ：俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京也在场。他在这次会议上的目标是什么？

articles.title: The AI boom had a really bad week — and it's raising loud alarms
articles.dek: A yearslong AI boom showed signs of unraveling this week in spectacular fashion.

paragraphs.en: A yearslong AI boom showed signs of unraveling this week in spectacular fashion.
paragraphs.zh: 持续多年的AI热潮本周以戏剧性的方式显现出衰退的迹象。

paragraphs.en: AI-related stocks have powered markets to record highs and helped support the broader economy. But investors now fear that a potential bubble in the sector could be bursting, which could spark wider financial repercussions.
paragraphs.zh: 与人工智能相关的股票推动市场创下历史新高，并有助于支撑更广泛的经济。但投资者现在担心该行业的潜在泡沫可能破裂，这可能会引发更广泛的金融影响。

paragraphs.en: Here's what to know about the week in AI and why alarm bells are ringing
paragraphs.zh: 以下是本周人工智能领域值得关注的动态，以及为何警钟正在敲响。

paragraphs.en: Investors were hoping the stock market debut of AI giant Anthropic this week would provide a boost to the markets. Instead, the entire stock market got pummeled on Friday, sparking one of the worst weeks that Wall Street has seen in quite some time.
paragraphs.zh: 投资者曾希望，人工智能巨头Anthropic本周的股市首秀将提振市场。然而，整个股市周五却遭遇重挫，引发了华尔街一段时间以来最糟糕的一周。

paragraphs.en: The tech-heavy Nasdaq dropped 10% for the week, its worst performance since the onset of COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns in March 2020. Even Anthropic, which gained 17% on its debut, ended up slumping more than 8% to close near its IPO price on Friday.
paragraphs.zh: 科技股为主的纳斯达克指数本周下跌 10%，这是自 2020 年 3 月新冠疫情封锁开始以来的最差表现。即使是首日上涨 17% 的 Anthropic，最终也下跌了 8% 以上，周五收盘时接近其 IPO 价格。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, both the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average entered a correction as of the close of trade on Friday, meaning a drop of 10% from their recent highs.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，截至周五收盘，标准普尔500指数和道琼斯工业平均指数均进入回调区间，这意味着较近期高点下跌了10%。

paragraphs.en: It's the culmination of weeks of fears that have been building up about the sustainability of the AI trade.
paragraphs.zh: 这是对人工智能板块可持续性数周来不断积累的担忧情绪的最终爆发。

paragraphs.en: Back in September, the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in over three years. That poses a big challenge to AI companies because they still need to borrow billions of dollars to do things like build out data centers that power the growth of their technologies. Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive for them.
paragraphs.zh: 早在9月份，美联储就迎来了三年多以来的首次加息。这对人工智能公司构成了巨大挑战，因为它们仍需要借贷数十亿美元来开展各种工作，例如建设数据中心，为它们的技术发展提供动力。利率的提高使他们的借贷成本更高。

articles.title: Google employees protest AI in schools policy
articles.dek: More than 550 Google employees signed a petition to allow schools access to Search without AI. Parents and educators protested outside Google offices in 6 cities last week for the same ask.

paragraphs.en: More than 550 Google employees signed a petition to allow schools access to Search without AI. Parents and educators protested outside Google offices in 6 cities last week for the same ask.
paragraphs.zh: 550多名谷歌员工签署了一份请愿书，要求允许学校使用不含人工智能的搜索功能。上周，家长和教育工作者在6个城市的谷歌办事处外举行抗议，提出同样的要求。

paragraphs.en: Parents and educators want Google to provide an AI-free version of the search engine for students. The backlash started after the company announced that they would not unbundle AI from their tools for education. Now some Google employees are joining in the push to provide AI-free access to students. NPR education reporter Sequoia Carrillo is following the story. She joins us now. Hey, Sequoia.
paragraphs.zh: 家长和教育工作者希望Google为学生提供无人工智能版本的搜索引擎。在该公司宣布不会将其教育工具与人工智能分离后，反弹情绪开始出现。现在，一些谷歌员工也加入到推动为学生提供无人工智能访问的行列中来。NPR教育记者Sequoia Carrillo正在跟进此事。她现在加入了我们的节目。嗨，Sequoia。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: So parents have mixed feelings, obviously, about using AI in the classroom. Why is Google taking such a firm stance on this?
paragraphs.zh: SCHMITZ：显然，家长们对于在课堂上使用人工智能持喜忧参半的态度。为什么Google在这方面态度如此坚决？

paragraphs.en: CARRILLO: I think mixed feelings is actually kind of a nice read of the situation. I've pretty much only talked to very angry parents, and we have a lot of very angry legislators, too, at the state and at national levels. Why Google's taking such a firm stance? There's no clear answer. I mean, some will point you to the fact that Google's very heavily invested in AI, and they want schools to be just as invested in it.
paragraphs.zh: CARRILLO：我认为“喜忧参半”其实是对当前情况的恰当描述。我几乎只和非常愤怒的家长谈过，在州一级和国家一级，我们也有很多非常愤怒的立法者。为什么谷歌要采取如此强硬的立场？没有明确的答案。我的意思是，有些人会告诉你，Google在人工智能方面投入了大量资金，他们希望学校也能像他们一样投入大量资金。

paragraphs.en: And I actually spoke to some people who pointed me towards two court cases earlier this year. Google got those dismissed by arguing that AI Overview and their search function are one tool. And those dismissals might mean that breaking them up could potentially be legally difficult for them. And when I talk to Google, they would not give us comments. So who is to say right now?
paragraphs.zh: 我实际上和一些人聊过，他们向我提到了今年早些时候的两起法院案件。Google通过辩称AI Overview和他们的搜索功能是一个工具，使这两起案件被驳回。这些驳回可能意味着，从法律上来说，将它们拆分可能对他们来说有难度。当我与Google沟通时，他们不愿向我们发表评论。所以现在谁能说得准呢？

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: That's really interesting. So it sounds like Google has sort of backed itself into a legal corner on this issue, and it sounds like Google's own employees are angry about this.
paragraphs.zh: SCHMITZ：这真有意思。听起来在这个问题上，谷歌似乎把自己逼进了法律的死胡同，而且谷歌自己的员工对此也很不满。

paragraphs.en: CARRILLO: Yes. So Google employees are now weighing in. A small percentage signed a petition to allow schools the option to use search without AI overview, and the union for Google employees says that they're worried that this could damage the company's reputation among students and teachers and end up with schools ultimately shutting out Google's products altogether. There is some merit to that. Earlier this month, we saw protests across the country outside of Google offices because of this exact stance.
paragraphs.zh: CARRILLO：是的。所以现在Google的员工正在发表意见。一小部分员工签署了一份请愿书，要求允许学校选择使用不带AI概览的搜索功能。Google员工工会表示，他们担心这可能会损害公司在学生和教师中的声誉，最终导致学校彻底弃用Google的产品。这种说法有一定道理。本月早些时候，我们看到正是因为这一立场，全国各地在谷歌办事处外发生了抗议活动。

paragraphs.en: SCHMITZ: So what are schools doing to prepare for this change?
paragraphs.zh: SCHMITZ：那么，学校正在采取哪些措施来为这一变化做好准备？

paragraphs.en: CARRILLO: People are definitely finding workarounds, and if they haven't already found it, they're definitely working on it. They say something as simple as the Chrome extension might be able to help districts keep the search engine. Fairfax County, a very large, well-funded district in Northern Virginia, was actually already doing this. They're piloting a kind of ad-blocking-type tool for AI on their school devices that they developed.

articles.title: Senate permitting bill speeds up renewables, divides greens over oil and gas
articles.dek: A permitting reform bill in the Senate could help speed the development of renewable energy projects, but it's splitting environmentalists over other provisions that help the oil and gas industry.

paragraphs.en: A permitting reform bill in the Senate could help speed the development of renewable energy projects, but it's splitting environmentalists over other provisions that help the oil and gas industry.

This week, the Senate passed a bipartisan bill that's meant to speed up construction of new energy infrastructure projects. It comes after midterm elections, when affordability and rising energy costs were top of the mind for many voters. But this bill divides Democrats and some of their key allies. NPR political reporter Matthew Brown joins us now. Matthew, thanks so much for being with us.
SIMON: So this bill is a rare example of bipartisan support. How did it come together?

BROWN: Well, lawmakers say they heard loud and clear that cost-of-living concerns are a top priority for Americans. This bill was co-sponsored by two Democrats and two Republicans and seeks to address those concerns by cutting or streamlining a lot of the regulations that many projects have to go through before they can be built. These are really complicated projects and can take years, sometimes even more than a decade, before they're finished. The idea is that if Congress cuts a lot of the red tape here, then more of these projects will be built, more energy will be produced and prices would then hopefully go down for Americans.
Here's one of the bill's authors, West Virginia Republican Shelley Moore Capito, talking up the bill on the Senate floor ahead of its final passage.

SHELLEY MOORE CAPITO: American people have used their voices, and they've made them clear. And we must listen. They deserve bipartisan solutions that make life more affordable. That's what this bill does.
SIMON: But, Matthew, how would this bill make life more affordable?

BROWN: Well, this would rewrite some of the nation's most important environmental laws - things like the National Environmental Policy Act, the Clean Water Act and the Endangered Species Act. It's really worth emphasizing these are bedrock protections that have been on the books for decades, and they were designed to make sure that things like animal species, local ecosystems and archaeological sites aren't damaged by development.

articles.title: Paolo Bulgari, who turned a family jewelry business into a global brand, dies at 89
articles.dek: ATHENS, Greece (AP) — Paolo Bulgari, the grandson of a Greek silversmith who helped transform the family jewelry business into a global luxury brand synonymous with Italian glamour and design, has…

paragraphs.en: ATHENS, Greece (AP) — Paolo Bulgari, the grandson of a Greek silversmith who helped transform the family jewelry business into a global luxury brand synonymous with Italian glamour and design, has died. He was 89.
His family announced his death Saturday, describing him as "the greatest jeweler of our time" and praising his humanity and entrepreneurial talent.
Bulgari presided for decades over a brand celebrated by supermodels, Hollywood stars and collectors for its bold designs and distinctive use of color.

Born in Rome in 1937, he was the grandson of Sotirios Voulgaris, who founded the jewelry business after leaving Greece. Originally from Paramythia, a mountain village in the Epirus region of northwestern Greece renowned for its silver jewelry, Voulgaris fled Ottoman rule and settled in Naples before opening a shop in Rome, adapting both his craft and his family name to his new home.

Paolo Bulgari joined the family business shortly after leaving school. Working alongside his father, Giorgio, he initially focused on precious stones, developing an expertise in gemstones that would inform his work as a designer and businessman throughout his career.

Turning away from the delicate aesthetic associated with Parisian jewelry houses, the Bulgari family embraced bold gemstones, rich yellow gold, generous proportions and unexpected combinations of color. Drawing inspiration from ancient Rome and Italy's artistic heritage, the distinctive style helped set the brand apart internationally.

Alongside his brother Nicola and nephew Francesco Trapani, Bulgari led the company's expansion into major luxury markets, opening stores in New York, Paris, Geneva and Monte Carlo. The business diversified beyond jewelry into watches, perfumes, leather goods and, eventually, hotels.

Heading the group since the mid-1980s, Bulgari guided the company through a period of significant international growth. Its jewelry was a fixture on celebrities spanning from Elizabeth Taylor to Zendaya. Tall and silver-haired, he occasionally appeared alongside the stars wearing his creations, maintaining a characteristically reserved presence.

articles.title: Another day of survival for a family in Ukraine
articles.dek: On the outskirts of Kyiv, one family prepares for the fifth winter of war against Russia — stockpiling food and fuel and trying to maintain as much a sense of normalcy as possible.

paragraphs.en: On the outskirts of Kyiv, one family prepares for the fifth winter of war against Russia — stockpiling food and fuel and trying to maintain as much a sense of normalcy as possible.
paragraphs.zh: 在基辅郊区，一个家庭正在为与俄罗斯交战的第五个冬天做准备——储存粮食和燃料，并尽量保持一种正常的生活状态。

paragraphs.en: For a fifth straight winter, Ukrainians fully expect that Russia will again attack their already weakened energy grid in an effort to break their will. But many Ukrainians are more determined than ever to hold on. NPR's Eleanor Beardsley spent time with one family outside Kyiv that has equipped itself for the worst.
paragraphs.zh: 连续第五个冬天，乌克兰人完全预计俄罗斯将再次攻击他们已经脆弱不堪的电网，以摧垮他们的意志。但许多乌克兰人比以往任何时候都更加坚定地要坚持下去。美国国家公共电台（NPR）的埃莉诺·比尔兹利（Eleanor Beardsley）与基辅郊外的一家人共度了一段时间，他们已经为最坏的情况做好了准备。

paragraphs.en: ELEANOR BEARDSLEY, BYLINE: It's dinner time at the Pavlenco household in the town of Irpin just north of Kyiv. The power is out and, the streets are dark across most of the Kyiv region. But the Pavlenco duplex is a pocket of warmth and light as parents Roman and Tanya make dinner.
paragraphs.zh: ELEANOR BEARDSLEY，署名：在基辅以北的伊尔平镇，帕夫连科一家正在享用晚餐。基辅地区大部分地方停电，街道一片漆黑。但帕夫连科家的双拼别墅却是一处温暖明亮的空间，父母罗曼和塔尼娅正在准备晚餐。

paragraphs.en: BEARDSLEY: Eggplant, mashed potatoes and pickled tomatoes from Roman's father's garden in Moldova. Roman, a doctor, now sells medical equipment. He's been in Ukraine for two decades, but he was born in Moldova on Ukraine's southwest border, which means he does not have to serve in Ukraine's military. So the family could leave the country, but they choose to stay.
paragraphs.zh: BEARDSLEY：茄子、土豆泥和腌番茄，来自罗曼父亲在摩尔多瓦的菜园。罗曼是一名医生，现在从事医疗器械销售。他在乌克兰已经生活了二十年，但他出生在乌克兰西南边境的摩尔多瓦，这意味着他不必在乌克兰军队服役。因此，这个家庭本可以离开乌克兰，但他们选择留下。

paragraphs.en: ROMAN: We are still at home. We are still in our country. I really trust that our country will survive, and I want that my children will live here because I want that my children will grow up like Ukrainians. Three sources - in the day from the sun, in the night from the batteries, and if we have from the central, we use that one.
paragraphs.zh: ROMAN：我有一整套系统。我的屋顶上装有太阳能电池板。还有就是这里的电池。第三，我还有来自中央电网的电。有三种来源：白天用太阳能，晚上用电池，如果有中央电网的电，我们就用中央电网的电。

articles.title: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year
articles.dek: NEW YORK — A bruising sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks on Friday pulled the S&P 500 down 3.7%, dragging the index to its worst weekly loss in more than 18 months, and knocking the Nasdaq…

paragraphs.en: NEW YORK — A bruising sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks on Friday pulled the S&P 500 down 3.7%, dragging the index to its worst weekly loss in more than 18 months, and knocking the Nasdaq composite into the red for the year.
paragraphs.zh: 纽约讯——周五，人工智能股遭遇重挫性抛售，导致标准普尔500指数下跌3.7%，创下18个多月以来的最大单周跌幅，并使纳斯达克综合指数今年以来转为下跌。

paragraphs.en: The benchmark index is now in what professional investors call a "correction," having fallen more than 10% from its Oct. 6 all-time high.
paragraphs.zh: 该基准指数目前正处于专业投资者所称的“回调”阶段，较10月6日历史高点已下跌超过10%。

paragraphs.en: The last time the S&P 500 had a correction was March 2025, as the Trump administration's trade war rattled the market. Its weekly loss, marking its worst such decline since April 2025, as the trade war escalated, capped a seven-day losing streak, the longest such string of losses since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
paragraphs.zh: 标普500指数上一次出现回调是在2025年3月，当时特朗普政府的贸易战令市场动荡不安。随着贸易战的升级，标普500指数的周跌幅创下2025年4月以来的最大跌幅，结束了七连跌的走势，这是自2020年新冠疫情爆发以来的最长连跌纪录。

paragraphs.en: The Nasdaq composite, which is more greatly influenced by tech stocks, slumped 5.3%, pulling it into negative territory for the year. Its weekly loss was also just shy of its worst week since March 2020, when the pandemic ground the global economy to a halt.
paragraphs.zh: 受科技股影响更大的纳斯达克综合指数暴跌 5.3%，跌入年度负值区间。其周跌幅也仅次于2020年3月以来的最差一周，当时新冠疫情使全球经济陷入停滞。

paragraphs.en: The Dow Jones Industrial Average, with less exposure to technology stocks, fell 1.9%.
paragraphs.zh: 道琼斯工业平均指数受科技股影响较小，下跌了1.9%。

paragraphs.en: Chip stocks like Nvidia, Micron Technology, Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices bore the brunt of the selling, but other companies connected to the AI buildout tanked as well, including the optical products company Corning and the energy provider Bloom Energy. The AI lab Anthropic, coming off a successful IPO Thursday, tumbled 9.1%.
paragraphs.zh: 英伟达、美光科技、博通和超威半导体等芯片股首当其冲，但与人工智能发展相关的其他公司也遭遇重挫，包括光学产品公司康宁和能源供应商Bloom Energy。人工智能实验室Anthropic周四成功上市，但股价随即大跌9.1%。

paragraphs.en: The sell-off in technology stocks spread around the globe: Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi each fell more than 5% overnight. European indexes fell sharply as well.
paragraphs.zh: 科技股的抛售蔓延至全球：日本的日经指数和韩国的科斯达克指数隔夜均下跌超过 5%。欧洲股市也大幅下挫。

paragraphs.en: AI stocks have hefty market values and have a much bigger impact on the market's direction. They were responsible for Wall Street's big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能股票的市值庞大，对市场走势的影响也大得多。它们是今年华尔街大涨的功臣，现在又成了市场大跌的幕后推手。

articles.title: Tech stocks end the week on a down note, despite Anthropic's mega-IPO
articles.dek: The stock market is ending the week down despite Anthropic's blockbuster IPO and a strong Nvidia earnings report, largely thanks to investor jitters about the future of AI.

paragraphs.en: The stock market is ending the week down despite Anthropic's blockbuster IPO and a strong Nvidia earnings report, largely thanks to investor jitters about the future of AI.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管有Anthropic的重磅IPO和英伟达强劲的财报，但股市本周仍以下跌收官，这主要归因于投资者对人工智能未来的担忧。

paragraphs.en: The stock market is ending the week down, way down. The tech-heavy NASDAQ has fallen 10% since last Friday. That is despite two really big events in tech that should have made investors feel pretty good. NPR tech correspondent John Ruwitch is here to walk us through the week. Hey, John.
paragraphs.zh: 股市本周收盘下跌，跌幅很大。自上周五以来，科技股为主的纳斯达克指数已下跌10%。尽管科技领域发生了两件非常重大的事件，本应让投资者感到相当振奋。NPR科技记者John Ruwitch将在这里为我们回顾本周行情。嗨，John。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: A quick note before we get into the story - Anthropic is a financial supporter of NPR, and we are obviously going to talk about Anthropic. So that being said, John, bring us up to speed on what's been going on in the stock market this week.
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：在进入正题之前，先简单说明一下——Anthropic是NPR的资助方，我们显然要谈到Anthropic。话虽如此，John，请向我们介绍一下本周股市的最新动态。

paragraphs.en: RUWITCH: Yeah, let me tell you about the first of those two events that you mentioned there that, seen through one lens or maybe some different quantum reality, could be seen as positive for the markets. It was Nvidia's earnings report. This is the most important chip company on Earth because it makes the most in-demand microchips that are powering the AI boom. Its quarterly financials on Tuesday were great. Its revenues were up over 100% from the same quarter last year, and the company raised its projection for next year's revenues. These are signs the company is doing very well.
paragraphs.zh: RUWITCH：是的，让我来谈谈你刚才提到的这两个事件中的第一个。从一个角度来看，或者从某种不同的量子现实来看，它可以被视为对市场有利的。那就是英伟达的财报。这是地球上最重要的芯片公司，因为它生产着最受欢迎的微芯片，这些微芯片正在推动人工智能的蓬勃发展。该公司周二公布的季度财务业绩非常出色。其收入较去年同期增长超过100%，公司上调了明年的收入预期。这些迹象表明公司经营状况非常好。

paragraphs.en: But, of course, this is a company in a state of turmoil, right? Founder Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO last week over allegations of marital infidelity, including with a woman who might have been spying for China. Now, those financial figures were baked in long ago - right? - before the scandal and before Huang was replaced by an interim CEO. The market didn't like it, though. Nvidia's share price is down over 20% from last Friday's close and nearly 40% over the past month as this saga played out.
paragraphs.zh: 但当然，这家公司正处于动荡之中，对吧？创始人黄仁勋上周因婚外情指控而辞去首席执行官职务，其中涉及一名可能为中国从事间谍活动的女性。现在，这些财务数据是很久以前就定下来的，对吧？是在丑闻发生之前，在黄仁勋被临时首席执行官取代之前。不过，市场并不买账。随着这场风波的演进，英伟达的股价较上周五收盘时下跌了20%以上，较上月下跌了近40%。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: So a complicated week, to put it mildly for an Nvidia.
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：对于英伟达来说，这周可谓相当复杂，这还只是委婉的说法。

paragraphs.en: DETROW: What about the second big event that investors were focused on?
paragraphs.zh: DETROW：投资者关注的第二个大事件是什么？

paragraphs.en: RUWITCH: ...The record-breaking IPO that this AI company had. It was the biggest in history. There was strong demand from institutional investors leading up to the IPO. The company was able to price its shares much higher than they had expected. And yesterday, on day one of trading to the public, its shares opened strong. They were 34% higher than the IPO price. That was all taken by some analysts as a sign that the AI trade is back and that there's robust demand for companies linked to AI.
paragraphs.zh: RUWITCH：……这家人工智能公司创下IPO纪录。这是历史上规模最大的IPO。在IPO之前，机构投资者的需求非常旺盛。该公司得以将其股票定价定得比预期高得多。昨天，在面向公众交易的第一天，其股价开盘强劲。比IPO价格高出34%。一些分析师认为，所有这些都表明人工智能交易已经回归，与人工智能相关的公司需求强劲。

articles.title: Trump's impact on an Ohio steel plant
articles.dek: The giant steel plant in Middletown, Ohio planned to switch away from using coke, a refined form of coal. The switch would have cut hazardous air pollution — and greenhouse gas emissions. But that…

paragraphs.en: The giant steel plant in Middletown, Ohio planned to switch away from using coke, a refined form of coal. The switch would have cut hazardous air pollution — and greenhouse gas emissions. But that plan has changed under President Trump
paragraphs.zh: 位于俄亥俄州米德尔敦的这家大型钢铁厂计划不再使用焦炭（一种精炼煤）。这一转变本可以减少有害空气污染和温室气体排放。但在特朗普总统执政期间，该计划发生了变化。

paragraphs.en: In Middletown, Ohio, a big steel mill is the city's largest employer and the biggest source of local air pollution. Under the Biden administration, the mill had planned to clean up its operations by shifting away from coal, but that has changed under President Trump. Middletown is now one example of the administration's efforts to boost fossil fuels. The Allegheny Front's Reid Frazier reports.
paragraphs.zh: 在俄亥俄州米德尔敦，一家大型钢铁厂是该市最大的雇主，也是当地最大的空气污染源。在拜登政府执政期间，该钢厂曾计划通过弃用煤炭来净化其生产运营，但在特朗普总统执政期间，这一计划发生了变化。米德尔敦现在是政府大力发展化石燃料的一个范例。阿勒格尼前线（Allegheny Front）的Reid Frazier为您报道。

paragraphs.en: REID FRAZIER, BYLINE: Donna Ballinger stands outside her house in Middletown, Ohio.
paragraphs.zh: REID FRAZIER，署名：Donna Ballinger站在俄亥俄州米德尔敦的自家门外。

paragraphs.en: FRAZIER: Through a thicket of trees, she points to the Middletown Works, a steel mill which rises several stories above her home.
paragraphs.zh: 弗雷泽：她指着一丛树林后面的米德尔敦钢铁厂，这座钢铁厂比她的家高出好几层。

paragraphs.en: FRAZIER: The plant makes steel the traditional way - using coke, a refined form of coal. That process emits a lot of air pollution, including carbon dioxide, which contributes to climate change. It also releases lots of soot, which drifts down onto Ballinger's neighborhood.
paragraphs.zh: FRAZIER：该厂采用传统方式炼钢，使用焦炭，这是一种精炼的煤炭。该工艺会排放大量空气污染物，包括二氧化碳，这会加剧气候变化。它还会释放大量烟尘，这些烟尘飘落到巴林格所在的街区。

paragraphs.en: BALLINGER: It's the fallout that's on everything we own, cars, property, kids' toys. You can't touch anything. You can't open your windows.
paragraphs.zh: BALLINGER：放射性尘埃落在我们拥有的所有东西上，汽车、房产、孩子的玩具。你什么都不能碰。你不能打开窗户。

paragraphs.en: FRAZIER: That soot is bad for human health. According to the EPA, the tiny particles are linked to higher rates of heart and lung problems, including asthma. Ballinger eventually got so fed up with the air quality, she began working with the local Sierra Club to try to force the plant to clean up.
paragraphs.zh: FRAZIER：这种烟尘对人体健康有害。根据美国环保署的说法，这些微小颗粒与更高的心脏和肺部疾病发病率有关，包括哮喘。Ballinger最终对空气质量感到厌烦，她开始与当地的塞拉俱乐部合作，试图迫使该工厂进行整治。

paragraphs.en: Then a few years ago, the steel mill did announce plans to cut its air pollution. Its owner, Cleveland-Cliffs, said it would convert to a new steelmaking process that doesn't use coal. Instead, it would switch to using natural gas or hydrogen. That would cut both the plant's local air pollution and its carbon footprint. That's important because the steel industry is a major source of climate pollution. CEO Lourenco Goncalves told investors at the time, hydrogen was the solution.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，几年前，这家钢铁厂确实宣布了减少空气污染的计划。其所有者Cliffs表示，将改用一种不使用煤炭的新型炼钢工艺。而是改用天然气或氢气。这将减少该厂的本地空气污染及其碳足迹。这一点很重要，因为钢铁行业是气候污染的主要来源。首席执行官Lourenco Goncalves当时对投资者表示，氢气是解决方案。

paragraphs.en: LAURENCO GONCALVES: We believe hydrogen will be the true game changer for the decarbonization of steel.
paragraphs.zh: LAURENCO GONCALVES：我们相信，氢能将成为钢铁脱碳的真正颠覆性因素。

articles.title: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
articles.dek: A federal judge in Virginia plans to issue a preliminary injunction blocking President Trump's triumphal arch indefinitely.

paragraphs.en: A federal judge in Virginia plans to issue a preliminary injunction blocking President Trump's triumphal arch indefinitely.
paragraphs.zh: 弗吉尼亚州的一名联邦法官计划发布一项初步禁令，无限期阻止特朗普总统的凯旋门项目。

paragraphs.en: District Judge Leonie Brinkema said during a Friday hearing that she would grant the request of the county board of Arlington, Va., which sued over the arch in October. Democracy Forward, the nonprofit representing the plaintiffs, confirmed the ruling in a statement shared with NPR.
paragraphs.zh: 地区法官Leonie Brinkema在周五的听证会上表示，她将批准弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿县委员会的请求，该委员会于10月就该拱门提起诉讼。代表原告的非营利组织Democracy Forward在与NPR分享的一份声明中确认了该裁决。

paragraphs.en: "We are pleased that the court has recognized the irreparable harm that will come to people who live and work in Arlington and stopped the massive vanity project while our case is heard and considered by the court," said senior counsel Kate Talmor.
paragraphs.zh: “我们很高兴法院认识到在阿灵顿生活和工作的人们将遭受不可挽回的伤害，并在法院审理和审议我们的案件期间叫停了这个庞大的沽名钓誉项目。”高级律师Kate Talmor表示。

paragraphs.en: Justice Department spokesperson Matthew Nies told NPR it will appeal the decision immediately.
paragraphs.zh: 司法部发言人马修·尼斯（Matthew Nies）告诉美国国家公共电台（NPR），司法部将立即对该裁决提起上诉。

paragraphs.en: The 250-foot arch would be built in Memorial Circle, which is part of D.C. but sits on the Virginia side of the Potomac River, a short distance from both Arlington National Cemetery and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, both in Arlington.
paragraphs.zh: 这座76米高的拱门将建在纪念广场（Memorial Circle），该广场属于华盛顿特区，但位于波托马克河的弗吉尼亚州一侧，距离阿灵顿国家公墓和罗纳德·里根华盛顿国家机场（均位于阿灵顿）不远。

paragraphs.en: Arlington County has argued that the arch would "cause significant harm" to its residents in multiple ways, including increasing noise and air pollution and "clogging thoroughfares needed for emergency transport services." And it said an arch that doubles as a military complex — as Trump has suggested — would pose public safety risks and require additional county resources to manage.
paragraphs.zh: 阿灵顿县认为，拱门将以多种方式对该县居民“造成重大危害”，包括加剧噪音和空气污染，以及“堵塞紧急运输服务所需的交通要道”。该县还表示，正如特朗普所建议的那样，一座兼具军事建筑功能的拱门将对公共安全构成威胁，并需要县政府投入额外资源来管理。

paragraphs.en: Arlington also argues the arch would disrupt historic sightlines between Arlington National Cemetery and D.C.'s National Mall, and pose logistical challenges for the roughly 24 to 27 funerals the cemetery holds every weekday. The county also has concerns about air and road traffic, saying construction-related delays could cause more accidents and disrupt emergency vehicles far beyond the traffic circle.
